articleTitle: Implementation of 5G Network Slicing Using Open Source Software
abstract: In modern communications, network slicing is essen-tial network operation for creating and managing an independent logical network which meets the requirement of a service. Net-work slicing enables available network resources to be managed and allocated efficiently and dynamically according to varying demands of users. This paper aims to design and implement 5G network slicing using open source software in order to serve very low latency services. The implementation requires the integration of orchestration, network function virtualization, and software defined network technologies to deploy necessary network functions and to manage the life cycles of network slices. Open source software tools such as Open5GS, Open Source MANO, OpenStack, OpenDaylight, and srsRAN are selected for implementing 5G core, orchestration and management functions, cloud computing platform, software defined network, and radio access network respectively since they offer compatibility in the software integration as well as allow the prototype to be created in a timely and economical manner. To obtain very low latency, User Plane Function and edge computing are implemented based on the latency of internal connections. In the experiment, different scenarios of network slices are deployed and tested to measure the key performance indices such as a delay, download speed and upload speed. The results show that the implemented network slices can offer very low latency at the expense of available bandwidth reduction due to the communication for orchestration and management in the hardware. However, this can be improved by using hardware with higher performance.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Tea Leaf Disease Identification Based on Convolutional Neural Networks VGG16, ResNet50, and DenseNet169 Image Recognitions
abstract: Tea is the most favorite drink in the world and its demand seems to continuously increase; therefore, large amount of tea production while retaining high-quality tea is required for the marketplaces. However, based on many research literacies, the yield and quality of tea are possibly affected by a diversity of diseases, which would need high accuracy in identification in order to determine the most suitable treatment or specific preventive actions. In this study, the tea leaf disease identification based on the three most widely used convolutional Neural Networks VGG16, Resnet50, and DenseNet169 were examined and evaluated. By accommodating the relevant parameters of these three identification models and the learning rates, the performances of the three convolutional neural networks were analyzed and compared. The simulated test results showed that VGG16, Resnet50, and DenseNet169 achieved the highest accuracy rates of 90.6%, 95.2%, and 99.0%, respectively. DenseNet169 provided the fastest convergence speed and the highest accuracy among the models. In addition, the DenseNet169 showed the possibility of the precise diagnosis and identification of other crop leaf diseases as well.

articleTitle: Construction of Position Telecontrol for Haptic Device Based on an Omnidirectional Mobile Robot
abstract: This paper presents the novel construction of a position telecontrol system for haptic devices based on an Omnidirectional Mobile Robot. Omnidirectional Mobile Robots are strategically stationed in various locations and used as haptic devices. Users can remotely control the movement of these haptic devices from various locations. The conventional PID controller is selected for position tracking control, and the Ziegler-Nichols closed-loop tuning approach is employed to adjust the parameter settings of all three controllers. Three experimental results confirm the controller's performance for position tracking telecontrol, demonstrating the achievement. The occurrence of steady-state errors is minimal, and a satisfactory level of overshoot is achieved.

articleTitle: A New Technique of Soluble NPK Nutrient Detection System Using Deep Learning-Based Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN)
abstract: Modern agriculture relies heavily on effective process monitoring, control, and remote data collection, making accurate and cost-effective sensors crucial for innovation. This research focuses on the development of a spectroscopy-based device for real-time and remote monitoring of nutrient levels in hydroponic systems. The device utilizes IoT architecture, incorporating principles of light absorbance to quantify concentrations of essential nutrients during crop growth. Three deep learning techniques, Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) were adopted for data analysis. Results demonstrate that tailored implementation of deep learning can significantly enhance the performance of sensor network system (SNS). Specifically, the RNN format achieved an impressive 98% model accuracy during both training and testing phases. The technological advancements in addressing contract variation and photometric levels contribute to increased accuracy as more sensors become available. The findings serve as a comprehensive guide for collecting extensive agricultural data, encompassing environmental factors throughout the entire cultivation period, using state-of-the-art remote control sensor equipment. This work provides a practical, efficient, and cost-effective solution for precise nutrient control and continuous data monitoring in agricultural production.

articleTitle: Meteorological Prediction Using Cloud's Images
abstract: This paper uses YOLO deep learning to create a predict system for Meteorological Service for Air Navigation with a total of 5 types of forecast results: BKN, CAVOK, FEW, OVER and SCT. Indicative information for evaluating the image is observing the nature of the clouds arranged together and comparing them to quantities in the sky using the unit of measurement “okta”, which is divided into 8 parts of the image. Therefore, the nature of using deep learning in the article is to teach deep learning to recognize various image characteristics both during the day and at night in order to use the results of the forecast to inform the weather conditions in the sky. The process in this article consists of 3 steps: The first step is to train the data with images with different characteristics from the 5 data types. The next step is to test the accuracy of the weights generated from the training and training steps. The final step is to use water values to create a decision-making system for users. From the experiment, private dataset in this paper, more than 2500 images were used to participate in the experiment. The results of the experiment found that the average results of precision, recall, mAP50, and mAP50-95 could be measured at 84.7%, 92.1%, 95.7%, and 95.3%, respectively.

articleTitle: Pragmatic Design of a Rectangular Printed Dipole Array Antenna for 5G Base Station
abstract: This paper presents the design, fabrication and measurement of a rectangular printed dipole array antenna for 5G base stations. The antenna element is composed of a rectangular printed dipole featuring a U-shaped gap and slot positioned atop a square reflector. The measured results of the prototype antenna exhibit good agreement with simulations. The impedance bandwidth of the antenna is noteworthy, covering a substantial frequency range of 3.00 GHz - 3.82 GHz, yielding a bandwidth of 23%. The maximum gains are 6.49 dBi at a frequency of 3.5 GHz. The half-power beamwidths (HPBW) in the x-z and y-z planes are obtained to be 101.45° and 22.44°, respectively, at the frequency of 3.5 GHz. These results underscore the effectiveness of the designed rectangular printed dipole array antenna, showcasing its suitability for 5G base station applications.

articleTitle: Tracking of Automated Guided Vehicle with 5G and UWB Real Time Location System in Smart Factory
abstract: Automated guided vehicle (AGV) tracking in a factory is considered as one of 5G use cases for Industry 4.0. In this work, a proposed AGV tracking system using ultra-wideband (UWB) radio technology for localization is installed in a manufacturing line. The tracking system can provide real time monitoring of AGV locations through web browser. When the AGV encountered a problem, it can be located quickly to resolve related problems and resume its operation much faster. The fifth generation (5G) cellular network provides a flexible production network such that the factory does not have to install local Wi-Fi network. 5G radio quality and network performance are measured. The benefits of 5G networks are listed and discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of 5G OFDM Frame Synchronization with Various Channel Conditions
abstract: This work presents a performance analysis of 5G OFDM frame time synchronization across diverse channel conditions. The research scrutinizes the impact of varying channel impairments, which are caused by multipath fading, and carrier frequency offsets (CFO), on the synchronization process. According to 5G standard, the primary synchronization signal (PSS) is used, which is distinguishable receiver, allowing it to correlate the received signal with the expected pattern and identify the correct timing offset for synchronization. The investigation quantifies synchronization error rates and pushes the boundaries of accuracy under realistic channel scenarios. The numerical simulations using MATLAB<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">@</sup> shows that the estimated timing frame synchronization has a high tolerance to additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and a Rayleigh communication channel and a CFO. Additionally, we propose that the system performance, such as MSE of the CFO and the BER comparison of the with various M-QAM order. Nevertheless, our proposed solution performs exceptionally well.

articleTitle: The Eccentricity Revelation Mechanism Based on FONDBMF for Consistent Sizableness Impulsive Outlier (CSIO)
abstract: In eccentricity revelation mechanism company, the depiction components are philosophically revealed as eccentricity or non-eccentricity components. This philosophical report scrutinizes the potency of the eccentricity revelation mechanism form on FONDBMF (First Order Neighborhood Decision Based Median Filter), which is upgraded from MDBUTMF (Modified decision based unsymmetric trimmed median filter) for resolving the deficiency of the foregoing eccentricity revelation mechanisms for CSIO at all consistency eccentricity (5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>-90<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>). In the examination section, innumerable outlier depictions, which are coalesced of Pepper and F16 at all consistency eccentricity, are examined by the eccentricity revelation mechanism form on FONDBMF in contemplation of verification of the potency of state-of-art schemes: SMF, MF, AMF and MDBUTMF. From these outcomes, the potency of the eccentricity revelation mechanism form on FONDBMF is superior than all state-of-art schemes at low consistency eccentricity in both PSNR index and visualization quality index.

articleTitle: Development of 5G Standalone QOS Tester Device for CAV Communication
abstract: Focus on Connected-Autonomous-Shared-Electric Vehicle (CASE), Connected and Autonomous Vehicle Technologies are a famous topic in the world. CAV requires high performance of communication links. 5G communication is a high-performance communication system in Thailand. The service area of 5G mobile communication in standalone mode increases every year. Quality of Service (QOS) in 5G for CAV is important. Commercial 5G QOS tester device is expensive. Then, the developing of 5G QOS Tester and QOS parameters in terms of radio and end parameters: SS-RSRP, SS-SINR, SS-RSRQ, RTT, Upload, Download, Jitter of 5G standalone for CAV are presented in this work. Our results confirm that 5G standalone is a high-performance communication link for CAV data transmission.

articleTitle: Optimal Load Scheduling for Smart Home Energy Management using Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This article presents an approach to optimal energy management in Smart Home Energy Management (SHEM) systems, utilizing the technique of optimal load shifting under the Time-of-Use (TOU) electricity tariff. The study employs Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) algorithms based on the Markov Decision Process (MDP), including Deep QNetwork (DQN), Advantage Actor-Critic (A2C), and Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). These techniques aim to identify optimal electricity load changes to minimize energy costs following the TOU tariff of the Provincial Electricity Authority (PEA). Simulation results show that using DQN, electricity costs decreased by 36.167% and the Peak Average Ratio (PAR) by 2.067 compared to the original load profile. However, the outcomes varied slightly among the different techniques, demonstrating that appropriate energy management in smart homes can effectively reduce electricity costs under the TOU tariff.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of IFFT-2048 Points for High Speed Transmitter OFDM Communication Systems with 64-QAM Mapping
abstract: High-speed wireless broadband technology mostly uses the modulation technology of orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) modulation format. This work presents a field programable gate array (FPGA) implementation of invert fast Fourier transform (IFFT) for OFDM with 64-QAM for WiMAX high-speed communication systems. The bandwidth of 400 MHz is considered. As a result, a 2.4Gbps (=6 bits x 400) speed rate can be achieved. A 2k (2048) according to the standard is used. Additionally, the efficient parallel Radix-2 computation algorithm is proposed. The proposed implemented Zynq UltraScale+ RFSoC board from AMD-Xilinx using vivado program version 2020. The process latency is 22,860 ns. The implementation results showed that the implementation is correct and that it achieves the expected performance. The resource consumption is only 7%. The number used as Memory is only 0.74%. The work can be adapted to implement a higher number point of samples in the IFFT algorithms.

articleTitle: Mathematical Modeling and Analysis of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor in Quaternion Space
abstract: This paper presents an innovative method for the mathematical modeling of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (PMSMs) using quaternion space. Traditional modeling methods typically assume a balanced three-phase voltage source, enabling the representation of the motor's rotation in a two-dimensional dq-space vector, with the third component set to zero. However, these conventional approaches prove inadequate when confronted with an unbalanced source, as the third component becomes non-zero, necessitating a three-dimensional model for precision. To address this challenge, quaternion space is utilized to formulate a mathematical model of the PMSM in three-dimensional space. In this study, all signals such as voltage, current, and flux are expressed as pure quaternions, and rotations in three-dimensional space are executed through quaternion multiplication. As a result, a mathematical model of the Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) is formulated within the realm of quaternion space. The construction of this quaternion-based model is intricately explained, providing a comprehensive representation of crucial aspects, including stator voltage, stator-rotor interactions, and critical parameters such as torque and power consumption. Simulation results demonstrate that the PMSM model based on quaternions exhibits behavior consistent with traditional models when subjected to a balanced three-phase voltage source. Notably, the developed model demonstrates adaptability in accurately representing the motor's response even in the presence of unbalanced stator voltage sources.

articleTitle: A Study on the Potency of Hybrid Models: Detecting Diseases in Cucumber Leaves with Pre-trained CNNs and SVM
abstract: This study investigates a hybrid machine learning approach for the classification of cucumber leaf diseases, combining the strengths of pre-trained Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Support Vector Machines (SVM). Focusing on a publicly available dataset, we evaluated four CNN architectures—VGG16, ResNet50, AlexNet, and EfficientNetV2—for feature extraction, followed by SVM for the final classification task. The performance of each model was assessed using F1 scores and confusion matrices, with ResNet50 yielding the highest F1 score, indicative of a strong balance between precision and recall. VGG16 and AlexNet showed potential for improvement, which could be realized through model tuning or integration into an ensemble framework. EfficientNetV2, despite a slightly lower F1 score, highlighted the importance of further training to enhance class distinction. The research underlines the importance of a hybrid approach, which harnesses deep learning's feature extraction capabilities with SVM's classification strength, to improve the accuracy of disease detection in cucumber plants.

articleTitle: Forecasting EV Market Trends in India: A Deep Learning Approach for Two/Three-Wheelers
abstract: This research paper presents a comprehensive analysis of machine learning models for predicting future sales of electric vehicles (EVs) in the Indian Market. With a specific focus on 2 and 3 wheeler sales. The study compares different machine learning approaches, including Linear Regression, Support Vector Regression (SVR), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) Neural Network, Through an evaluation of their respective errors, LSTM Neural Network method demonstrates superior prediction accuracy, making it the preferred model for forecasting EV sales, specifically 2 wheeler and 3 wheeler sales over the next five years. The paper aims to present the forecasted sales figures, in hopes of providing valuable insights into the future trajectory of EV sales and serving as a vital resource for stakeholders in the electric vehicle industry.

articleTitle: A Simple Real-Time Traffic Light Control System using PLC
abstract: This paper presents a simple real-time traffic light control method using the PLC model CP1L-M30DR-A. The control system can be operated and monitored through the HMI model EA043A. The traffic light control model represents a simple intersection with a single lane road, featuring traffic flow in four different directions. Each direction is equipped with a single traffic light. Initially, the duration of the green traffic light for all four directions was set at 30 seconds, with the option to extend it to a maximum of 90 seconds. On each road, two inductive proximity sensors were installed to measure the density of passing vehicles and the numbers of vehicle waiting at red traffic lights. The collected data is transmitted to PLC to calculate the green traffic light duration. Specifically, when the traffic density exceeded 15 cars, the duration of the green traffic light was extended by 1.6 seconds per car. The results obtained from the real-time control test proved to be accurate.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Battery Capacity Tester with Online Monitoring for Educational Use
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are conventionally used as power supplies of portable electric devices (such as mobile phones and laptops) due to their small sizes, affordability, and long cycle lives. However, the capacity of LIBs gradually decreases from their rated value (referred to as capacity fading) depending on the number of charge cycles. Inaccurate LIB capacity estimation leads to imprecise state-of-charge (SoC) estimation, negatively impacting energy management capabilities. Conventional battery capacity testers presently on the market are expensive and lack Internet of Things (IoT) capabilities for storage and monitoring. Therefore, this study presents a low-cost battery capacity tester with online monitoring for educational purposes. This tester offers two discharging levels of 0.5 A and 1 A. Additionally, a temperature sensor has been integrated to monitor the battery's temperature and prevent overheating. The tester employs an ESP32 module as the main microcontroller, and the Arduino IoT Cloud system is used to store measurement data in a cloud database. The voltage and current during testing can be conveniently displayed on a computer or mobile phone through an associated graphical user interface (GUI). Two LIBs were subjected to testing at both discharging levels to validate the capabilities of the tester. The experimental results revealed a maximum error of 1.7% and a minimum error of 0.25%.

articleTitle: Development of Innovative Virtual Media Set for Learning Renewable Energy
abstract: The research aims to develop an innovative virtual media set for learning renewable energy. Research tools include a teacher's manual, a learning assessment form, and a virtual media package for learning about renewable energy, consisting of solar cell systems, wind power systems, and hydroelectric system simulators. The research process is divided into four steps: 1) studying the principles of virtual media development, 2) defining the designed framework, 3) developing innovative virtual media, and 4) evaluating the media performance. The research findings revealed testing of electricity-generating packages for solar cell power, wind power, and hydropower systems. It can perform close to actual and theoretical working conditions. The five experts' viewpoints on appropriation in utilizing the virtual media set for learning renewable energy were highly suitable, and the ten users' satisfaction was also high level. Finally, the innovative virtual media set for learning renewable energy can be used effectively in the learning and teaching science and technology courses.

articleTitle: Ozone Treatment Strategies for Efficient Color Removal in Wastewater
abstract: This paper presents a thorough analysis of the application of ozone generators in wastewater treatment processes. The study delves into the intricate systems involved, which encompass key components such as a high-voltage power supply, electrodes, and a dielectric material composed of glass. The strategic implementation of this glass dielectric material is aimed at mitigating direct electrical discharge. Mesh electrodes, exemplified by stainless steel corona electrodes, play a pivotal role in facilitating the ozone generation process. The generator is systematically supplied with air through an air pump, a recognized strategy that contributes to enhancing ozone production efficiency. At the heart of the ozone generation process lies in the corona discharge, initiated by the application of a high voltage-typically in the range of thousands of volts-across the electrodes. This process induces air breakdown at 25 kV/cm, with the potential for reduced voltage requirements through the introduction of additional glass dielectric material. The applied voltage stimulates a corona discharge around the corona electrode, leading to the breakdown of oxygen molecules (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O_{2}$</tex>) into individual oxygen atoms. These oxygen atoms subsequently combine with other oxygen molecules to generate ozone (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O_{3}$</tex>). The produced ozone is then seamlessly introduced into wastewater for treatment, underscoring its pivotal role in water purification processes. This comprehensive investigation emphasizes the indispensable importance of ozone generators in wastewater treatment, presenting a promising avenue for the development of efficient and environmentally friendly solutions for water treatment processes.

articleTitle: A Study on 1D-Point Cloud Using Through-Wall mm Wave Radar for Human Pose Estimation
abstract: This paper presents human pose estimation using millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar technology capable of penetrating obstacles. Operating within the frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) at 60 - 64 GHz, our radar system generates signals conducive to accurate human pose representation. Our data processing framework focuses on producing point cloud data, effectively capturing each human movement. Results are visualized through a 2D graph, with the z-axis representing time. Experimental data, collected from various activities conducted behind different walls, underwent thorough analysis, comparing point cloud positions with actual human postures. The outcomes affirm the effectiveness of mmWave radar systems, positioned behind obstacles, in accurately extracting human postures.

articleTitle: Improved Three-Level Boost Converter to Balance Duty Cycles for Fuel Cell and Photovoltaic Applications
abstract: This article acknowledges the current serious global pollution problem. While appreciating efforts to bring in renewable energy from sources such as solar panels and fuel cells, it is important to recognize that both types of energy cells have limitations in their output voltage. To overcome this limitation, the use of a three-level boost converter has been proposed. Although this is an interesting solution, there are still limitations in terms of the unevenness of the switching duty cycle. This results in unequal potential differences across the switching devices. The result is an uneven heat buildup inside the device. For this reason, the article proposes a new approach. By combining a “three-level boost converter” with an interleaved boost converter, this innovation balances the switching duty cycle of every switch. As a result, the system works more efficiently and sustainably.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Forex Trading: Leveraging Keras Sequential Models and Optimized Features to Maximize Profitability
abstract: The research presented here focuses on evaluating a predictive model's performance by leveraging diverse input features extracted from Forex price charts. A series of experi-ments explore a range of parameter settings, with assessments conducted across 30 distinct Forex symbols. The research involves utilizing OHLC (Open, High, Low, Close) data and a historical dataset of 100 candlesticks to predict price movements. It employs a trading algorithm for initiating BUY or SELL orders based on opening and closing prices, yielding suboptimal results. However, through further investigation, the study combines the MACD in-dicator and Hammer candlestick pattern, demonstrating that this integration of indicators effectively reduces noise and enhances model accuracy. It underscores the importance of continuous relearning when employing the model and recommends high-spec computer equipment. Notably, Model 3 achieved substantial profits during a 1-year and 4-month backtest.

articleTitle: Exploring CST Simulation Techniques for TEM Mode and Unit Cell Analysis to Determine Refractive Index
abstract: The study investigates the accuracy of CST simulations in TEM mode and unit cell simulations for determining the refractive index (n) of materials. The results in TEM mode align with the expected properties of air, affirming the correctness of settings. However, when using unit cell simulations, the materials properties template inaccurately calculates n values, deviating from reality. Further examination reveals that unit cell simulations emit waves of different modes (TE, TM, or CP) instead of TEM, leading to inconsistencies. A revised equation is introduced to address this discrepancy, yielding results closer to actual n values. The importance of parameters like D and m is emphasized, as variations significantly impact the n values obtained. The introduced equation provides more accurate n cal-culations in unit cell simulations than the default CST template.

articleTitle: Dual-Mode Dual-Band Filter Using Steppedimpedance Resonator with Outer Tuning Plus-Sign
abstract: This article introduces a dual-band filter employing a folding structure of stepped-impedance resonator with an outer tuning plus-sign. The design integrates a meandered square loop resonator (SIR), with patches positioned at each corner of the square loop to induce a dual-mode response. Furthermore, the second frequency can be fine-tuned by adjusting the outer tuning plus-sign located outside the meandered loop. A dual-mode dual-band filter is designed with the first frequency at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.4\text{GHz}$</tex>, featuring a loss of insertion of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.58{{\ dB}}$</tex>. The first frequency exhibits transmission zeroes beside the upper and lower frequencies of the middle frequency, resulting in a sharp skirt. The second frequency, designed at 5.2 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{GHz}$</tex>, has a loss of insertion of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.59{{\ dB}}$</tex> and a return loss better than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$- 15{{\ dB}}$</tex>. The design and analysis are validated using the IE3D simulator.

articleTitle: A Robotic Arm for Sorting Metals and Non-metals Controlled by PLC and Microcontroller
abstract: This paper presents an automated robotic arm designed for sorting of objects into metals and non-metal base on their weight. The system is controlled by an FX3U-32M PLC and an Arduino Mega 2560 microcontroller. The robot arm utilizes an AC servo motor to drive its spindle, a linear slide rail for vertical movement, and a ball screw driven by a DC motor for horizontal arm motion. An inductive proximity sensor is used to differentiate metals. The object weight is determined using a load cell, which is compared with a specified reference weight entered via a keypad. This weight comparison is pre-processed by the microcontroller to interface with the PLC. The robot arm can move vertically up to 15 centimeters, horizontally up to 35 centimeters, rotate up to 180 degrees, and manipulate objects weighing up to 0.55 kg. Based on the experimental results, the robotic arm can accurately and precisely classify objects into metal and non-metal categories and by their weight and separate them in various pre-defined positions.

articleTitle: Imaging Conductivity Distribution of Ventilation with Single-frequency and Frequency-difference Electrical Impedance Tomography
abstract: Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT) is a technique to image the conductivity distribution that has been used in many medical applications. For lung application, EIT can image lung ventilation with a good temporal resolution which is helpful for diagnosis and providing information for lung recovery. The image reconstruction of EIT is usually based on a single excitation frequency. The reconstruction also usually uses a common chest model instead of an exact chest model due to limited availability resulting in a modeling error in the reconstruction process. In this study, the change in conductivity of frequency difference was investigated whether it can be used for lung ventilation monitoring. A method to construct a frequency difference image was proposed. Some techniques to reduce the influence of modeling error were also investigated whether they could improve the reconstruction or not. An experiment result on a subject showed that the frequency difference method can be used for monitoring the respiration activity with higher discriminability i.e. the conductivity change in each lung region was clearly seen. However, the single-frequency method still provided a better shape of the change that was consistent with the lungs' shape. The implementation of the modeling error reduction could significantly increase the image amplitude for both methods, but it could reduce the artifacts for only the single-frequency method.

articleTitle: Small Loop Antenna Arrangement Investigation for 350 kHz Through-the-Earth Communications in Limestone Cave
abstract: This paper proposes the arrangement investigation of the small loop antenna for Through-the-Earth (TTE) communications in limestone cave. Specifically designed with a 1/50 wavelength at the operating frequency of 350 kHz for cave use. The measurement setup consists of a transmitter system located at the surface station on a mountain and a receiver system at an underground station within the limestone cave at Wat Tham Phra Phothisat, Saraburi, Thailand. The signals are transmitted from the surface transmitter with an earth-grounded antenna, propagating through the earth to reach the small loop antenna with the receiver underground. We investigate the arrangement of the array and the increase of the small loop antenna element from one to four elements. From the measurement results, we found that a vertically oriented single small loop antenna effectively receives signal power from the earth-grounded antenna. Moreover, the increasing of elements to the small loop antenna enhances its capacity to receive higher signal power, with the optimal arrangement being a 4×1 vertical array antenna that exhibits an increase of approximately 19.2 dB when compared with the single small loop antenna.

articleTitle: Comparing the Coordinate-Sequencing for Human's Joints Models on Thai Finger Spelling
abstract: Video-based sign language recognition plays a crucial role in enhancing communication and accessibility for those who are deaf or hard of hearing. However, developing and maintaining high-quality sign language datasets from video input is difficult, especially in Thai, because of the lack of a standard Thai finger spelling video dataset. To overcome this challenge, this article must focus on accumulating a larger total of 42 primary alphabets in Thai Finger Spelling from 22 signers with various appearances and genders. We conduct four deep learning-based archi-tectures: a sequence of coordinates of joints in human's body using LSTM, BiLSTM, GRU, and Transformer models. Indeed, we compare their performance under three scenarios of single-hand posture: single-stroke, two-stroke and three-stroke poses. Our results reveal that Transformer has the greatest performance on both in-sample and out-of-sample test sets.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of Single-Shunt Diode RF Rectifier Using Electromagnetic Co-Simulation
abstract: In this paper, an efficient design process for a single-shunt diode RF rectifier is proposed. The technique focuses on tuning microstrip line sections in electromagnetic and circuit co-simulation. The design study can achieve an RF-to-DC conversion efficiency of 51.27% at the center frequency of 950 MHz with -10 dBm input power. Good agreement between full wave electromagnetic simulation and electromagnetic/ circuit co-simulation is demonstrated, providing substantial support for the proposed RF rectifier design technique.

articleTitle: The Fault Detection Method for a DC Traction Rectifier Substation in Mass Rapid Transit Railway Systems
abstract: Reliability and safety are the critical issues for electric railway systems. The regulated DC voltage of 750 V for the traction substation is generated by a three-phase PWM rectifier with the appropriate controller design. Under the occurrence of faults in the three-phase PWM rectifier the desired performance of the electric railway system cannot be maintained. Therefore, the three-phase PWM rectifier is required to operate properly under fault tolerant conditions. In this paper, the fault detection method for the open-circuited switch fault of the three-phase PWM rectifier is proposed to enhance the fault tolerance requirement. The behavior of the three-phase PWM rectifier in both normal and fault modes is investigated. The proposed fault detection method relies on the measured values used for the controller without additional sensors. The simulation results implemented by the MATLAB SIMULINK software package show the effectiveness of the proposed method to detect a fast and accurate fault occurred in the three-phase PWM rectifier.

articleTitle: Classification of Snatch Weightlifting Phases
abstract: Weightlifting is a sport in which competitors compete by lifting a barbell loaded with weight plates from the floor with the goal of successfully lifting the heaviest weights. The snatch is the first event completed in weightlifting competitions. This work studied the classification of snatch weightlifting phases using images, posture landmarks and object detection. We used the Open Source Computer Vision Library (OpenCV) to extract the images from weightlifting videos. CNN, ResNet50 and VGG16 were applied to classify the phases of snatch weightlifting from the images. In addition, MediaPipe and You Only Look Once (YOLO) were studied to extract posture landmarks of athletes' bodies and barbell features from weightlifting images. The accuracy of 91.96% was achieved using the Support Vector Machine (SVM) with the posture landmarks and barbell features. The VGG16 classifier achieved the highest accuracy of 92.26%. The accuracies from the first to the sixth phase were 98.50%, 98.05%, 99.25%, 99.32%, 94.59% and 94.82%, respectively.

articleTitle: Hybrid Power Management with Fuzzy Logic
abstract: This The system controls solar energy and electrical energy from the engine into the water pump for agriculture. This system occurs because some agricultural areas still do not have electricity. This system uses a combination of solar panels and an engine to generate electricity. And this system uses batteries to provide additional electricity at night. Solar panel systems will have an uncertain output power. It depends on the intensity of sunlight and insufficient water pumping power. Therefore, the system has a generator to compensate for the power from the solar panel system. At the same time, the operation of the engine depends on the energy stored in the batteries, since most of this energy is needed for pumping water for agriculture. An optimized fuzzy inference system diagram is used to forecast time series of solar radiation values. A metaheuristic algorithm is used to determine the appropriate membership function and rules for the fuzzy inference tree.

articleTitle: Pilot-Assisted Channel Estimation for SFBC MIMO-OFDM with Index Modulation in Higher Time-Varying Fading Channel
abstract: Orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) with Index modulation can provide higher spectral and energy efficiencies. For multiple-input, multiple-output OFDM with space-frequency block coding (SFBC MIMO-OFDM), the transmitter can send the information signal with high transmit diversity gain to the receiver, improving system performance. In this paper, we propose a pilot-assisted channel estimation by using SFBC MIMO-OFDM with index modulation. The proposed system can perform a better bit-error-rate (BER) performance and higher transmission data rate than the conventional system in a higher time-varying fading channel.

articleTitle: Water Level Monitoring and Flood Alerting by Applying IoT
abstract: A flood is a natural disaster that causes problems in many aspects, resulting in subsequent losses. Thailand can reduce flood impact with an early warning system, allowing time for prevention. This project was created to develop a flood warning system according to the early warning system project of the Department of Water Resources. The project emphasizes informing local residents to better understand the situation and more quickly assess solutions and responses. By installing the water level measuring units at the point near the people's residence, the people can choose to install it themselves, which can transmit the data from the base to the main control unit that monitors the house of the residents in that area by applying ultrasonic sensors and rain detection modules that are controlled by a microcontroller. There is a multi-channel notification system, both light and sound notifications. Displaying messages on the LCD screen and notifications via the Line application. The remote control also uses the Blynk application to reset the main control station and all three bases. Including having a ThingSpeak data recording system to analyze the situation and later cut off power within the households. The results of the experiment can show good notifications.

articleTitle: Thermal Insulated Leakage Current Measurement using a Fluxgate Sensor with an Aerogel Insulation for DC Charging Applications
abstract: The fluxgate current sensor exhibits temperature drift due to its thermal sensitivity, which could affect the accuracy of leakage current measurement; especially, when using for the large variation of temperature and heat in DC charging applications. This paper proposes an improved thermal insulated fluxgate current sensor by using an additional aerogel insulation sheet wrapped around for the sensor. The proposed sensor model was formulated based on the Jiles-Atherton B-H hysteresis model and was solved with the fourth order Lunger Kuta method. The mathematical model was optimized to account for the effect of temperature. Detailed analysis of the temperature drift of conventional fluxgate sensor compared to the proposed one with an aerogel thermal insulation sheet with respect to enhance sensor performance in DC charging pile conditions was presented. The simulation results indicated that the proposed thermal insulation fluxgate current sensor effectively suppressed the temperature drift and thus could achieve safer and more reliable operation of the DC charging pile and offers compared to the conventional sensor.

articleTitle: Deep Convolutional Neural Networks for Accurate Solar Module Classification in Thermal Images
abstract: The rapid and continuous technological advancements in computer and internet technologies, combined with data management techniques, find applications in various domains. For example, they aid in predictive maintenance systems, evaluate the performance of solar modules, and differentiate efficiently performing solar modules from less efficient ones using thermal imagery. The accuracy of solar module classification significantly impacts the subsequent assessment. In this study, we employ advanced techniques, particularly deep learning through Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), to classify thermal images of solar modules. The practical aspects of applying CNN to the dataset of thermal images are explored, including transfer learning from pretrained CNN architectures and custom CNN architecture training. Experiments are conducted with three prominent types of solar module conditions: normal, cracked, and dusty. The results reveal that the most effective approach involves learning and fine-tuning pre-trained architectures on detailed studies, achieving a classification accuracy of up to 94.5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>.

articleTitle: CRF-Named Entity Recognition Model for Ancient Isan Medicine Texts
abstract: Manually extracting named entities from ancient Isan medicine texts is time-consuming and requires specialized expertise. Currently, there are no machine learning models specifically developed for this purpose. To bridge this gap, this research paper presents a Named Entity Recognition (NER) model built upon the Conditional Random Field (CRF) method. This model identifies and classifies the names of medicines, diseases, and herbs within these documents. It achieved an accuracy of 96 percent. Additionally, the model was utilized to develop the named entity recognition application. The assessment of this application indicated that is performed at the highest level in all assessed aspects.

articleTitle: The Mathematical Model Analysis of PV Panel Using Python
abstract: This article presents a comprehensive exploration of computer methods that leverage open-source Python modules to extract key parameters for the mathematical model of the single-diode equivalent circuit of a PV panel. The electrical performance of a PV panel is analyzed in response to variations in solar irradiance intensity and PV module temperature, providing valuable insights into its behavior under varying environmental conditions. The methodology employed enables the calculation of I-V (current-voltage) and P-V (power-voltage) curves based on the single-diode model. Additionally, it demonstrates how to visualize these curves, enhancing the understanding of a PV panel's performance. Utilizing the Kyocera KC200GT module as a case study, the results confirm the effectiveness of this approach, offering valuable insights not only to electrical engineering students but also to solar energy system engineers and researchers.

articleTitle: Predicting Dota 2 Game Period Winners Through Hero Analysis
abstract: The impact of hero selection on game outcomes is well-recognized, with input from respected streamers and commentators who emphasize the significance of hero choices. These insights, supported by substantial followers and views, underscore the importance of astute hero selection. However, hero selection is not straightforward due to factors like player proficiency and team strategy. While extensive game data allows us to gauge hero performance, practical challenges exist. To address these, a method for real-time outcome prediction based on hero selection is introduced. This approach includes an interface for hero selection, displays sections for hero information, and identifies both winning and losing heroes. The method also calculates and displays the financial advantage in-game, a crucial factor, and adapts to evolving patches, ensuring its reliability and accessibility to players.

Author Keywords: Hero Selection and Impact on Game Outcomes

articleTitle: Optimal EV Charging Control for Distribution System Loss Minimization
abstract: This paper proposes the methodology for optimal EV charging scheduling (OEVCS) using particle optimization (PSO). The goal of this work is to minimize the total energy losses of the distribution system. The proposed PSO-based OEVCS was tested by the IEEE 33-bus system with modifications to include the charging load of the EVs. Simulation results show that the proposed EV charging scheduling method can minimize the total daily system energy losses.

articleTitle: Estimation of Object Position and Orientation for Dimmable Visible Light Positioning
abstract: This work investigates how to estimate the position as well as the orientation of an object in an indoor environment with Light Emitting Diode (LED) ceiling lamps that may be independently dimmed. A receiver with three Photo Diodes (PDs) and angular diversity is used to measure Received Signal Strengths (RSSs) with respect to each LED lamp. To support light dimming, these RSSs are normalized and used to estimate the orientation angle relative to each LED lamp. In particular, the normalized RSS vector is compared in terms of the cosine similarity with the RSS reference vectors for orientation angles of 0, 1,…, 359 degree. Based on these relative orientation angles, the receiver position as well as its absolute orientation (with respect to the positive y-axis) are next estimated using the least square error criterion. Simulation experiments with nine LED lamps on the ceiling of a room (10 m wide, 10 m long, 2.75 m high) and random object positions and orientations at the height of 0.75 m from the floor show that, for 90% of the time, the position error is within 0.6 m while the orientation error is within 4 degree.

articleTitle: A DGS-Based Ultra Wideband THz MIMO Antenna for Wireless Communication
abstract: The increasing need for high data rate communication and sophisticated imaging technologies has spurred the exploration of ultra wideband Terahertz (THz) Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) antennas. The circular segment added circular two-port THz antenna that operates between 2.9 and 11.1 THz is presented in this work. The proposed THz MIMO antenna has an overall geometry of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20\times 46\times 2\mu \mathrm{m}^3$</tex>. The suggested THz MIMO antenna is made on a polyimide substrate that is 2 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> thick and has a relative permittivity of 3.5. The antenna's radiator and ground plane are modified by integrating parasitic components to accomplish the proper operating frequency and isolation. The antenna's interport isolation is improved to exceed 20 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{dB}$</tex> by employing a redesigned ground plane as a decoupling structure. Upon examination, the proposed antenna's MIMO diversity properties are determined to be ECC <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< 0.0$</tex>, DG <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\approx 10\text{dB}$</tex>, TARC <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< -10\text{dB}$</tex>, CCL <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< 0.2\text{bps}/\text{Hz}$</tex>, and MEG <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< -3\text{dB}$</tex> over the antenna's impedance bandwidth. According to the diversity parameters result, the suggested MIMO architecture is suitable for applications involving wireless communication.

articleTitle: Unmilled Rice Moisture Content Sensor for Rice Mill Factory Applications
abstract: This research presents a novel electromagnetic-based sensor for inline measurement of unmilled rice paddy moisture content in the rice mill factory. The proposed sensor has been designed based on the modified planar dipole structure at the operating frequency of 440 MHz. The unmilled rice dielectric constant properties have been studied and applied for characterizing the moisture content. The unmilled rice moisture content sensor system then has been designed consisting of the proposed sensor, a microwave signal generator, a microwave signal detector, and a microcontroller. The moisture content sensor system has been implemented and used for measuring the unmilled rice paddy moisture content in a real rice mill factory in Udon Thani province, Thailand. When compared with the commercial rice moisture content tool based on a capacitance technique, the proposed rice moisture content sensor system gives almost same results, which only about 4% difference has been found.

articleTitle: Deployable Wideband Circularly Polarized S-Band Antenna Array for CubeSat Applications
abstract: A broadband circularly polarized (CP) S-band antenna array for CubeSat technology was proposed. The proposed CP antenna array comprised of 2 × 2 rectangular-shaped ring patches and sequentially rotated feeding structure. Besides, the sequentially rotated feeding structure is utilized to match impedance. This antenna is made of single-layered Roger RT5880 substrate. The simulation results at 2 GHz achieved IBW of 81% (1.3 – 2.92 GHz) and ARBW of 25% (1.85 – 2.35 GHz). The optimal RHCP gain is 4.69 dBic at 2.25 GHz. The half-power beamwidth at 2 GHz is 71.51∘. The radiation patterns are RHCP characteristic. The proposed CP S-band antenna array with sequentially rotated feeding structure is deployed with the CubeSat platform, resulting in the proposed CP antenna array befitting CubeSat technology.

articleTitle: DC-DC Buck Converter with Adaptive Gain for Improving Line Transient Response
abstract: The dc-dc buck converter is widely employed to lower the output voltage below the input voltage, offering low ripples in both current and voltage due to its output filter properties. However, abrupt variations in the input supply voltage can lead to line transients, resulting in significant output voltage fluctuations. These fluctuations can potentially damage downstream equipment and cause disruptions. This study aims to enhance the line transient response of a dc-dc buck converter in voltage mode control. To improve the line transient response of a dc-dc buck converter, this study introduced an additional adaptive gain into the voltage control loop. Simulation results demonstrated that the proposed approach exhibited minimal undershoot and overshoot in the output voltage, even in the presence of variations in the input voltage.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of Dynamic Wireless Battery Charging System for Electric Vehicles
abstract: Dynamic wireless battery charging systems for electric vehicles (EVs) have the potential to charge EVs while in motion. This can extend the driving range and a small capacity of battery can be used which reduces the vehicle's weight. However, the performance of this system depends on the magnetic coupling coefficient between coupled coils and vehicle's speed. To investigate these issues, this paper presents the experimental study of the dynamic wireless battery charging system for EVs. It consists of five experiments including the static wireless power transmission to a resistive load, dynamic wireless power transmission to a resistive load, dynamic wireless battery charging, and dynamic wireless power transmission to the running motor of EVs. All experiments are discussed in detail which leads to the exploration of the dynamic wireless battery charging system for electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Design of All Textile Ultra-Wideband Monopole Antenna for Wearable Applications
abstract: This paper proposes the design of all textile ultra-wideband (UWB) monopole antenna. The textile antenna structure includes of the octagonal-shaped patch and modified ground plane. Conventional rectangular ground plane is modified as curve-shaped ground plane with circular parasitic patch. By using this ground plane structure, it can shift the lowest edge of impedance bandwidth to lower frequency and enhances the directivity. The textile antenna can provide a compact size having dimension of 35 × 40 × 1 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. Based on simulation, the impedance bandwidth of antenna is 138% (2.36-12.78 GHz) and maximum gain is 5.19 dBi at 7 GHz. The textile antenna achieves very wide bandwidth covering ISM band and UWB which is suitable for wearable applications.

articleTitle: Sequential Channel and Phase Noise Equalization for 5G OFDM Communication Systems
abstract: This paper presents a step-by-step analysis of the wireless communication channel and phase noise compensation for fifth-generation (5G) orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM). The performance of least squares using cubic spline interpolation technical. Additionally, to ensure optimal OFDM operation, phase noise requires cancellation, employing the common phase noise method. Performance is evaluated using bit error rate (BER), and a numerical simulation method is employed in MATLAB. The simulation result showed that the performance of estimates and phase noise correction is acceptable, it has a lower BER than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup> and uses channel taps that aren't more than 200 taps so that OFDM system processing has performance.

articleTitle: Deep Multimodal-Based Recognition of Thai Finger Spelling with Two-Handed Postures
abstract: Video-based recognition of sign language is essential in improving communication and access for individuals who are deaf or have hearing impairments. The sign language encompasses two primary categories: single-hand and two-hand signs. Two-hand Thai sign language poses learning and communication challenges, including the difficulty of mastering hand coordination and the complexity in interpreting these gestures, especially by automated systems, leading to potential misunderstandings. To overcome this challenge, this paper presents a new novel large video dataset for two-hand poses of Thai Finger Spelling. Moreover, we propose the multimodal technique for RGB-sequencing-based modality on CNN-LSTM and VGG- LSTM models and the graph structure on skeleton modality using Temporal Graph Convolution Network (TGCN) under two scenarios: (1) static point-on-hand poses and (2) dynamic point-on-hand poses. Our result shows that the single modality is unsuitable for two-hand poses due to hand obstructions, which stem from insufficient coordinate sequence data or lack of feature extraction in the vision modality. To improve the accuracy and performance of two-hand postures, the study suggests combining RGB-sequencing with the vision modality and graph structure with the skeleton modality.

articleTitle: Analysis of Constant Switching Frequency Quasi-Resonant ZVS-ZCS Boost Converter using State-Plane Diagram
abstract: Two novel quasi-resonant zero voltage switching (ZVS) and zero current switching (ZCS) combined boost converters under constant switching frequency operation are proposed in this research work. With both MOSFETs working under pulse width modulation (PWM) and soft switching conditions, the proposed circuits are able to operate at high switching frequencies with low switching losses and a small component size. The state plane diagram method will be applied for the converter analysis. Converter design as well as computer simulation for analysis validation is presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Sintering of Cu-TiCN Electrode Materials for Electrical Discharge Machining Process
abstract: Electrodes are an important tool in the Electrical Discharge Machine (EDM) production process to produce samples in the desired shape, Produced in large quantities with a smooth surface. There is a low wear and wear rate. In the production of electrodes mixed with other materials and copper. Using the sintering process as another option in the process of producing electrodes. This research studies the production of titanium carbo-nitride (Cu-TiCN) composite electrodes that have been sintered at a temperature of 1,250 “C” using a compression molding force of 22 “Mpa” that affects work efficiency, which has different percentages of ingredients from testing, it was found that a mixture ratio of Cu 80%, Ni 3%, TiCN 17 % is the best ratio for producing electrodes. Has a hardness value of 112.8 “HV” wear-resistant. It has a minimum electrical resistance value of 0.40148 “Ω.cm” a value that allows electric current to flow through it the best. It has a density value of 6. 9 8 “g/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>” indicating good adhesion, resulting in a minimum porosity value of 8.386 %. Along with examination with the SEM process, it was found that there is a strong bond between the molecules that makes them stay together in large groups the most.

articleTitle: The Efficaciousness of the Outlier Reclamation Scheme Established on a First-Order Recursive FIR Linear Predictor for Salt&Pepper Outlier
abstract: Typically, the concomitant outlier reclamation scheme, which is ideologically integrated of an outlier unmasking scheme and an outlier reclamation scheme, is an obligatory pre-computing scheme that has to be operated before other sophisticated image processing schemes. As a result, a First-Order Recursive Linear Finite Impulse Response Linear Predictor (FRL-FIRLP) that has been evolved from a pioneer median filter (SMF) has been asserted for Salt and Pepper noise at great propagation. This technical essay addresses to interrogate the efficaciousness and limitation of a FRL-FIRLP scheme, which offers the statistical concept of reclamation of the noisy component by using a linear predictor established on ARMA (Auto Regressive Moving Average). In the computer verification section, countless noisy decorations, which are integrated of Lena and Girl at great propagation, are used to verify the efficaciousness of the outlier reclamation scheme established on FRL-FIRLP scheme. A correlation of the efficaciousness is made with countless current schemes (Median Filter (SMF), Mean Filter (MF), Adaptive Median Filter (AMF)) in terms of visional and measurable aftermaths (PSNR and SSIM).

Author Keywords: A First-Order Recursive Linear Finite Impulse Response Linear Predictor (FRL-FIRLP)

articleTitle: The DC Voltage Controller Design of Traction Substation in Heavy Rail Systems
abstract: The DC voltage for the traction substation is normally generated from the electricity authority via twelve-pulse diode rectifier. As a result, the DC voltage is not constant depending on the load. In this paper, the three-phase two-level six-switch boost-type rectifier is introduced for the traction substation in which the DC voltage can be regulated to 750V for all operations. Moreover, the proposed rectifier can allow the energy from the train regenerative braking back to the electricity authority as well as the PV arrays in the future. The details how to design the controllers for the active front-end rectifier are explained in the paper. The simulation results from the exact topological model of MATLAB are used to show the effectiveness of the new architecture of traction substation in heavy rail system.

articleTitle: Testability Considerations for Custom Processing-In-Memory Cores
abstract: In this paper, test considerations and challenges for Processing-In-Memory (PIM) cores are presented and discussed. PIM provides the integration of a local Processing Unit (PU) with RAM (Random Access Memory) on a single Integrated Circuit (IC). This approach to digital system implementation provides the ability to alleviate data transfer rate limitations between the PU and RAM by reducing the timing delays between the processor and memory through a reduction in interconnect delays, and delays introduced by intermediate logic, seen in a traditional processor-memory interfacing approach. However, with new circuit and system architectures, along with higher levels of integration requiring the use of lower geometry fabrication processes, comes the need to effectively and efficiently test the circuits and systems. This paper considers different Design for Test (DfT) approaches and available standards to support test and DfT. In this paper, an IEEE (Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers) standard 1500 wrapper is developed to allow the PU and memory to be tested both in isolation and when operating as a single PIM core.

articleTitle: Fuse-Saving Strategy Using Back-to-Back Converter for Microgrid
abstract: The fuse is commonly coordinated with other protective devices to prevent a long interruption caused by blown fuse during temporary faults. This paper proposes the fuse-saving strategy using back-to-back (BTB) converter for microgrid. The BTB converter, which is an interface between microgrid and main grid, has the recloser capability coordinating with the fuse. This fuse-saving strategy does not require the recloser installation. The investment and maintenance costs of recloser can be removed. Moreover, the time-current characteristic (TCC) of recloser capability is properly varied to avoid the miscoordination caused by distributed generator (DG) fault current contributions. According to the simulation results, the proposed fuse-saving strategy can prevent the damage of fuse during temporary fault. The voltage level and frequency of microgrid are also restored to the nominal values after the fault is extinct.

articleTitle: Eliminating Insignificant Periods in Forex Analysis for Accurate Results
abstract: In this research, we conducted an extensive analysis using a dataset comprising over 48,000 data points to determine optimal period values for 30 different symbols. Our investigation covered four distinct timeframes for each symbol, including H1, H4, D1, and W1. The comprehensive results of our study are presented in Tables 2 to 7 for reference. The application of this information is straightforward. For instance, if we need to configure the Period for the EMA indicator within the D1 time frame for the GBPUSD currency pair, considering an acceptable percent error of 3%, we can refer to Table 4. It provides an appropriate Period value for the GBPUSD D1 currency pair, which is 38. This value can then be utilized as the Period setting for the EMA indicator or other relevant indicators.

articleTitle: Broadband Fabry-Perot Cavity Antenna with Two-Layer Partially Reflective Surface Using Periodic Structures
abstract: This paper presents a high-gain and wideband Fabry-Perot cavity antenna (FPCA) utilizing a two-layer partially reflective surface (PRS). The PRS composed of periodic unit cells, featuring a cross-dipole slot etched on a square patch. The antenna is intended to operate within the frequency spanning from 5.15-6 GHz for V2X communications using WLAN-based or cellular-based standards. The positive reflection phase gradient, an important characteristic required for a wide gain bandwidth produced by the suggested PRS. A feed antenna consists of a rectangular with a split U-shaped patch and an outer rectangular ring to achieve a wide impedance bandwidth. The parameter study of PRS was conducted using a simulation software to obtain the best performance. The simulation results show that the present FPCA achieves the broadside gain with maximum of 12.9 dBi and a 3-dB gain bandwidth of 10.51%, represent a 7 dB gain improvement over the feed antenna alone. In addition, the impedance bandwidth ranges from 4.92 to 6 GHz, which covers the desired operating frequency range.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Application for Precise Identification of Defective and QC-Approved Tablets in Pharmaceutical Manufacturing
abstract: Distinguishing between quality and substandard tablets is vital for public health, patient safety, and regulatory adherence. Stringent healthcare and pharmaceutical regulations underscore the importance of medication safety and quality. Establishing the legitimacy of medications builds trust, fortifying a resilient health care system essential for effective medical care and societal welfare. Hence, this paper employs the You Only Look Once (YOLOv7) model for the real-time identification of defective and QC-passed tablets, achieving a notable overall accuracy of 97.5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> in our successful experimentation.

articleTitle: SUTH-BME-FindmE: Determine Real Time Position of Medical Devices in a Large Hospital
abstract: Locating medical devices within a large hospital presents a challenge. Biomedical Engineers (BME) often traverse multiple floors in search of these devices for daily preventive maintenance. To address this, wireless access points have been installed on every floor of each building in the hospital. In response, a distance-based approach that utilizes both fingerprinting and trilateration techniques has been chosen. This research aims to develop a cost-effective technology for locating medical devices in large hospitals. Two configurations, one Device Under Test (DUT) per medical device and three DUTs per medical device, are proposed. Our findings indicate that trilateration combined with fingerprint techniques can be implemented affordably with improved position estimation. However, positioning errors may vary depending on the indoor environment.

articleTitle: Algorithm to Identify Peaks in Trading Charts
abstract: Traders rely on accurate peak detection to analyze market patterns and predict future prices. While the zigzag indicator is favored by most traders for its effectiveness, applying it to low volatility data, like MACD charts, leads to distorted peaks. Similarly, mathematical algorithms may generally find peaks, but these are often deemed inaccurate by traders due to the inclusion of insignificant points. Consequently, this research introduces a peak filtering algorithm tailored to traders' needs, aiming to refine peak identification. The algorithm is successful in filtering out significant peaks, as demonstrated in Figure 8, addressing the limitations of existing methods.

articleTitle: Adaptive Orthogonal Gradient Algorithm Based on Fair Cost Function
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive orthogonal gradient algorithm with the unconstrained Fair cost function. An adaptive orthogonal gradient-based algorithm is investigated with the help of orthogonal projection mechanism to update the approximate tap-weight vector for the convergence enhancement. Fair cost function is preferable with a smooth points that is able to detect the statistical characteristics of error. Objective of this work is to present an adaptive orthogonal gradient algorithm using Fair cost function (OGA-Fair) to enhance the performance. Simulation results show that proposed adaptive OGA-Fair algorithm can perform with the fast convergence rate and robustness better than the existing method.

articleTitle: Application of Adaptive Image Enhancement Method for Mammogram Enhancement
abstract: Enhancing mammograms plays a critical role in improving contrast, thereby aiding radiologists in the accurate diagnosis of breast cancer. This study introduces a novel approach that combines low illumination techniques, a color image correction approach grounded in nonlinear functional transformations based on the illumination-reflection model, and multiscale theory to effectively enhance mammographic contrast. Initially, the 2D mammogram is transformed into a 3D representation for enhancement and subsequently transformed to the HSV color model. The illumination component of the V channel is extracted using multiscale Gaussian functions. Adaptive adjustments are then applied to the image improvement function parameters for both S and V channels based on the distribution profiles of the illumination elements. Furthermore, an image fusion method is devised to extract details from both images, followed by conversion from HSV to RGB space. Finally, the RGB image is complemented to obtain an enhanced image. Experimental findings demonstrate that the suggested approach significantly enhances mammographic contrast while mitigating oversaturation issues observed in bright regions when compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: Automated Voltage-Ratio Measurement for Resistance Calibration
abstract: The development of an automatic calibration system is conducive to getting very effective measurement results and convenient use, especially for resistance calibration by using the voltage-ratio method based on Ohm's law. By this method, the referent current is biased through two resistors (known and unknown resistors) to evaluate the voltage ratio value. Based on the comparative ratios of voltage and resistance values, the unknown resistance can be calculated. Therefore, the high stability of the referent current bias and the simultaneous voltage measurement between two resistors should be considered. In this work, an automatic calibration system is developed via LabView for resistance calibration using the referent current in the range of 1 µA to 200 A. The developed software can work effectively based on the software validation. The stability of the bias current is within the instrument manufacturer's specifications measured by the developed software.

articleTitle: A Multi-Level Inverter Using Single-Carrier PWM and DC Levels Shifting
abstract: This paper presents a multi-level inverter using a single-carrier PWM (SCPWM) and dc level shifting. The proposed system uses the H-bridge topology for cascading and constructing the output voltage. The proposed system has two parts; the first is a high-speed switching to support the SCPWM, and the second is a low-speed with 7 modules for dc level shifting. These two parts are combined to construct the ac voltage output at 17 levels and the output ac voltage regulation is controlled by the PI controller from 0V to 271V with a frequency in the range of 40-65 Hz. A detailed proposed topology analysis is presented and verified followed by simulation results to verify the advantages of the proposed converter system.

articleTitle: Development of the Function Check Stability of Digital Media Receivers using Interference Mitigation Techniques
abstract: This study explores techniques to mitigate interference in assessing functions related to AM radio wave signals in digital media receivers. Signal transmission cable testing focused on BNC RG59 75-ohm cables with length of 300 mm. Six methods were employed: Method 1 used a Ferrite core, Method 2 used copper tape, Method 3 connected a grounding wire, Method 4 combined grounding wire connection with a Ferrite core, Method 5 combined grounding wire connection with copper tape, and Method 6 combined grounding wire connection with both a Ferrite Core and copper tape. The result has been shown that Method 6 yielded optimal results, with AM 1000 kHz Usable Sens, AM Interstation Noise L, and AM Interstation Noise R functions differing from reference values by −3.53 dBm, −5.05 dBm, and −5.26 dBm, respectively, emphasizing its efficacy in enhancing the assessed functions.

articleTitle: Small-Signal Stability Analysis in an Uncertain Microgrid with Distributed Energy Resources: A Data-Driven Monitoring
abstract: In low-inertia microgrids (MGs) with intermittent distributed energy resources (DERs), the requirement to pre-determine MG parameters results in a challenge as these parameters evolve over time. Consequently, conducting small-signal stability analysis becomes impractical due to the dynamic nature of the MG's parameter variations. In this paper, we propose an adaptive data-driven approach designed for grid-forming converters of DERs. The goal is to improve small-signal stability within a dynamically shifting window range. Additionally, we propose a data-driven approach to identify the MG model within a moving window. Subsequently, small-signal stability can be assessed. Comprehensive simulation results are systematically generated for an MG with DERs under various crucial conditions, including (i) intermittent power outputs of DERs, (ii) generator outages, (iii) diverse levels of total MG inertia, and (iv) different MG operation modes.

articleTitle: Nighttime Energy Management Strategy of All-Electric Ship during Berthing
abstract: During nighttime, due to no sunlight, the photovoltaics (PVs) installed on all-electric ship (AES) cannot be used for charging battery and supplying loads. Thus, the nighttime energy management is important to beneficially utilize the battery placed on AES. This paper proposes the energy management strategy of AES berthing at night. During berthing, if the seaport power system is disconnected from the utility grid, the battery and inverter installed on AES cooperate to maintain the voltage of AES distribution system. In case of shore-side unsymmetrical fault, the inverter installed on AES is used to compensate the unsymmetrical voltage sag by injecting the reactive current. According to the simulation results, during seaport power system disconnected from utility grid, the proposed strategy can keep the voltage of AES distribution system at the nominal value. Moreover, during shore-side unsymmetrical fault, the unsymmetrical voltage sag is effectively compensated while the voltage in the nonfaulty phase is not affected.

articleTitle: Optimal Daily Scheduling of Hybrid Wind-Hydrogen Storage using Particle Swarm Optimization
abstract: This paper proposes a particle swarm optimization-based optimal daily scheduling (PSO-ODS) for hybrid wind-hydrogen storage (HWHS). Minimizing daily energy loss (DL) is the main goal of the presented method. The approaches of PSO-ODS for HWHS were inspected with the modified IEEE 33-bus system with HWHS integration using load and wind profiles of Thailand. The studies are separated into two cases, which are the wind-integrated system with and without hydrogen storage optimal scheduling. The proposed approach can effectively decrease DL for the HWHS integrated distribution system, as indicated by the simulation results.

articleTitle: Single-mode Dielectric Resonator Bandpass Filter without Internal Coupling Iris
abstract: This research proposes a single-mode dielectric resonator bandpass filter. Designing a rectangular dielectric resonator involves drilling a hole at the center of the structure to shift the spurious frequency away from the initial frequency. This approach configures the external Qe of the resonator as an I/O coaxial probe. The internal coupling between two resonators is easily adjusted without irises between two resonators. The filter circuit was designed using the HFSS simulator as a secondorder circuit at a frequency of 1.95 GHz, with a 3-dB fractional bandwidth of 3.59% (70 MHz). The passband insertion loss is less than 0.04 dB, and the return loss is better than 22.46 dB in the passband.
