articleTitle: Effect of Span 80 Surfactant in Transformer Oil-Based TiO2 Nanofluids on the Electrical Properties of Lightning Impulse Voltage
abstract: This article aims to investigate the impact of varying quantities of Span 80 surfactant on the mixture of transformer oil and nanoparticles. This article has chosen to use semiconducting titanium dioxide (TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) nanoparticles at a concentration of 0.01 wt.% of the volume of mineral oil. The effects of surfactants at 0%, 50%, 60%, 70%, 80%, 90%, 100%, and 110 wt.% of the nanoparticle content will be looked at in this study. The endurance of lightning impulse voltage was assessed by conducting tests on the electrical characteristics of both positive and negative poles, in accordance with international standards. The results are also compared with those of traditional transformer oil test results. The test results indicated that transformer oil was blended with TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanoparticles at a concentration of 0.01 wt.% and Span 80 surfactant was added at a quantity equivalent to 90 wt % of the nanoparticle content to assess durability against positive and negative lightning impulse voltages. Moreover, compared to transformer oil mixed with TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanoparticles and surfactants in any amount, it has better resistance to lightning impulse voltage, performing better than regular transformer oil.

articleTitle: Energy Consumption Analysis of NB-IoT for Very Large Sensors
abstract: Narrow Band Internet of Things (NB-IoT) is a low-power wide-area network (LPWAN) technology, which is used in many IoT applications. Additionally, it is also widely used for real-time monitoring systems. This paper presents an energy analysis of NB-IoT, where a number of sensors per node is large. In this case, the power very critical. The analysis considers the different power-saving features of NB-IoT, such as extended discontinuous reception (eDRX), power saving mode (PSM) and type of battery. The results of the analysis show that research findings indicate that the number of sensors values (either 15 or 30) and the battery type have a minimal impact on energy consumption. Concerning battery life, VRLA batteries outperform LI-PO batteries, enabling longer operational periods. In conclusion, the battery type significantly influences the NB-IoT device's usage duration, with VRLA batteries proving more suitable for extended use compared to LI-PO batteries. NB-IoT can significantly reduce the energy consumption of large amount of sensors.

articleTitle: Developing Smart IoT Systems to Control Peak Demand Energy Using ESP8266 for Split Type Air Conditioners
abstract: This research presents an energy management approach to achieve the appropriateness between energy consumption and energy demand. This is to achieve the most cost-effective energy consumption. By applying the technology that exists today for this reason, programmable IoT system has been developed. NodeMCU / ESP8266 can be connected to a smart config Wi-Fi network. The developed system found that the system design that used to control on-off and temperature control in the room to reduce power and cost especially load split type air conditioners. on-off control conditions split type air conditioning is the number of people entering-exiting. And the appropriate temperature in the room according to the actual use of split type air conditioners can save electricity 77 kWh per day about percentage 33 of electricity consumption percent from normal use is load management for the demand side in order to be sufficient for the supply side for smart grid system in future.

articleTitle: HTTP/2 Web Performance Characteristics with Link-aggregation Mode Under DDoS Attack
abstract: The HTTP/2 Web server is widely used in Internet service. Furthermore, attacks known as distributed denial-of service, or DDoS, were popping up online. HTTP/2 not only allows multiple requests per connection but also protects against DDoS attacks. This paper focused on network link aggregation for bonding multiple Gigabit Ethernets of an HTTP/2 physical machine. Also, we used four link-aggregation modes with no special network switch support, including Round-Robin (Mode 0), Load Balance (balance-xor) (Mode 2), Balance-TLB (Mode 5), and Balance-ALB (Mode 6). We evaluate h2load performance under 3 Gigabit/s DDoS attacks. The results show that Round-Robin (Mode 0) can be served over HTTP/2 as a normal service during a DDoS attack. In addition, Balance-ALB (Mode 6) can be serviced like Mode 0, but this mode has lower performance compared to normal service. However, Mode 2 and Mode 5 can't be served while DDoS attack sizes exceed 20 KB. This paper can conclude that only round-robin mode can protect against DDoS attacks. Although HTTP/2 can protect against DDoS attacks, it can also work after link aggregation

articleTitle: Power Pool vs P2P Energy Trading Mechanisms: A Social Welfare Perspective
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study of Power Pool and Peer-to-Peer (P2P) energy trading mechanisms from a social welfare perspective. Focusing on the evolving landscape of energy trading, particularly amidst the integration of renewable energy sources, this study utilizes linear programming and a multi-stage matching mechanism (MMM) to analyze and compare these two models. Our findings reveal that while the P2P model facilitates a greater volume of energy transactions, the Power Pool model achieves higher social welfare. This contrast highlights the distinct strengths and weaknesses of each market mechanism. The research underscores the importance of developing criteria for an efficient comparison between the two models and contemplates the inclusion of additional variables like carbon credits and the impact of geographical proximity on renewable energy trading. The study contributes to a deeper understanding of these trading mechanisms, providing insights crucial for shaping future energy markets.

articleTitle: Optimal Number of Wires for Circuits on RTLDesigned FPGAs
abstract: FPGAs (Field-Programmable Gate Arrays) with reconfigurable features are used in various applications. However, circuits on FPGAs are inferior to circuits on ASICs in operating frequency, power consumption, and area. Co-design of FPGA and ASIC is one way to solve this problem. To realize this co-design, RTL-Designed FPGAs have been proposed by the authors. The features of the FPGAs are that they can be described only with HDL and that they can be realized with ordinary standard cells. Therefore, FPGAs and ASICs can be co-designed easily. Until now, the FPGAs have not been considered for optimal wiring count. In this paper, we clarify the optimum number of wires using a 4-bit adder circuit. In addition, cases in which more than that optimal number of wires is needed are discussed.

articleTitle: Optimization for Initialization in Unfalsified Control
abstract: Unfalsified control stands as a prominent approach amidst various adaptive controller design methods. Its key advantage lies in its independence from the need for a precise plant model. Nevertheless, a significant challenge arises when initiating the algorithm without prior knowledge of the system model. This paper presents a novel strategy for obtaining an initial offline controller to generate preliminary off-line plant input and output data. Subsequently, these datasets can be leveraged with a selection of your preferred artificial intelligence techniques to identify the first optimal controller. Subsequently, we generate the remaining candidate controllers to meet the requirement of having a finite number of candidates. Furthermore, we demonstrate a method for establishing the initial set of unfalsified control, which can be effectively deployed in real-time applications.

articleTitle: IoT System for Greenhouse Monitoring
abstract: This paper presents the implementation of an automated system that can monitor environmental and plant parameters in a greenhouse. A series of sensors connected to a Raspberry Pi collected temperature, air humidity, and atmospheric pressure parameters. Plant monitoring is done through a high-quality Raspberry Pi camera with a wide lens and a near-infrared (NIR) filter. The fusion of visible and near-infrared images calculates the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) to study plant health. A sliding assembly with X-axis movement allows image capture for multiple plants. The movement is done using a stepper motor controlled by the Arduino Uno development board. The entire system is remotely controllable via the IoT Greenhouse web application. Access to the application is conditioned by authentication, thus protecting the collected data.

articleTitle: Investigation of Fuel cell tied Unified Filter towards grid resiliency for future smartgrid
abstract: Due to the growing amount of variable renewable energy, the power grid's dependability and stability depend on new power conditioners that make sure customers get smooth, consistent energy delivery. These conditioners are critical in producing power that not only fulfils high standards of quality but also maintains a balanced voltage and current to reliably satisfy demand. This is valid in both balanced and unbalanced settings, emphasising the need for power conditioners in stabilising energy supply from various sources. This study investigates the application of a Unified Power Quality Conditioner employing a Fuel Cell as the DC source for a Neutral-Point-Clamped multilevel inverter. This configuration is designed to address power quality challenges that occur with the inclusion of green energy sources in the power network. Separate control methodologies were implemented to create controllers for each level. Synchronous Reference Frame (SRF) theory provides a framework for controlling a Neutral-Point-Clamped (NPC) multilevel inverter, enabling its function as a power quality conditioner. This work proposes a UPQC for mitigating issues such as voltage sags and swells that disrupt the operation of the system. By integrating a PI control loop to ensure precise control of the DC link voltage, minimizing voltage fluctuations. The functionality of the proposed controller was verified through the utilization of MATLAB/Simulink simulations that encompassed a wide range of operating conditions.

articleTitle: Microgrid Voltage Stability Indices Improvement Using Particle Swarm Optimization
abstract: This paper provides a strategy for improving microgrid voltage stability indices (VSI) using particle swarm optimization (PSO). The L-index value is used to assess the weak bus of the system. The IEEE 33-bus system is used for evaluating the proposed method, including four cases as follows; the IEEE 33-bus base case, the IEEE 33-bus with L-index improvement, the IEEE 33-bus as microgrid (MG), and the modified IEEE 33-bus as microgrid with L-index improvement. For VSI improvement, PSO is utilized to determine the generator bus voltages for minimizing the L-index. The proposed method can successfully minimize the L-index for both conventional distribution networks and MG systems, from the simulation results.

articleTitle: Generalization of Modular Three-Level Buck Converter
abstract: This paper proposes a three-level buck converter that can feed numerous loads from a single input source. The circuit is built in the form of N modules, which allows for the usage of switches and input capacitors with voltage ratings lower than the input voltage source. This can lower the cost of constructing the circuit. General equations in an ideal case for the proposed circuit are also provided to aid with calculations and module implementation.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Efficiency Enhancement for a Solar Panel Using Water, Ice and Dry Ice Backside Cooling Systems
abstract: The purpose of this research is to study and conduct an experimental test for investigating the increase of efficiency of a solar panel when cooling it with a backside cooling system. There were 3 experiment test-rigs by using 3 different refrigerants: water, ice, and dry ice. By containing a type of refrigerant into its identical box that was designed by wrapping insulation around the box while drilling the holes for the box that did not contain any refrigerant. Then covered the box with a solar panel. To determine which refrigerant could be the best helped increase the efficiency of a solar panel. The research team conducted the tests with 2 time periods: a short time for 1 hour operation when collecting experimental results for every 2 minutes and a long time for 6 hours when collecting experimental results every 10 minutes. It is found from the experimental tests that significantly different capacity in power generated for different types of refrigerants could be obviously noticed even for the short time. For the long-time test, ice was the best refrigerant that continuously enhanced the efficiency for the solar panel with 25.2 watts compared with 24.0 watts for no refrigerant cooling, which was 6.25% increase.

articleTitle: Optimizing Maximum Profit for Electric Vehicle Users in a Bipolar DC Distribution Grid with Probabilistic EV Load Demand and V2G Integration
abstract: This article delves into the synergistic potential of integrating Bipolar DC distribution grids, Probabilistic EV load demand forecasting, and Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technology. It offers a blueprint for electric vehicle (EV) users to smartly improve their financial results. Through the amalgamation of these components, individuals who possess electric vehicles have the potential to mitigate their energy expenditures while concurrently generating additional income. The study reveals that the integration of EV into the distribution system can lead to a substantial increase in daily energy loss, reaching up to 25.91%. However, when V2G technology is employed within the distribution grid, it has the remarkable capability to mitigate this increase in daily energy loss significantly, achieving a reduction of up to 64.12%.

articleTitle: Analytical Models and Evaluation for Novel Multi-Stage Flywheel Configurations for Grid-Connected Wind Power Applications
abstract: Flywheels are one of the commonly used devices for energy storage for grid-connected wind power systems. However, using large and heavy flywheels for high power storage applications could encounter some problems when installed in the areas with large variation of wind speed. This paper proposed a novel approach of multi-stage flywheel configurations where several sub-flywheels were used to extract the power from different levels of wind speed. There were 2 staging types proposed, an identical multi-stage flywheel and an incremental multi-stage flywheel. Their analytical models were first developed, following by the performance evaluation tests in the MATLAB-Simulink program compared to the conventional bulky flywheel. The case study of 6kWh energy storage was considered and thus allowed a stage of 6 identical l kWh sub-flywheels and a stage of 1 k Wh, 2kWh and 3kWh flywheels for identical and incremental multi-stage flywheels, respectively. The test results showed that the incremental multi-stage flywheel provided optimum benefits among high energy storage capacity, large wind speed variation operation and optimum system complexity.

articleTitle: The Development for Diabetic Retinopathy Lesion Detection on Fundus Photography
abstract: This research aims to advance the accuracy and precision of diabetic retinopathy lesion identification on retinas through the utilization of fundus photography, particularly from the publicly available Kaggle database, consisting of a total of 35,126 images. The image processing workflow involves four steps for enhancing the quality of low-quality retinal images. These steps include histogram matching for image sharpness adjustment, contrast enhancement for improving image clarity, noise removal using a median filtering operator, and optic disk localization for identifying and removing the optic disk boundaries. Data analysis is conducted using two techniques: K-means clustering algorithm and Mathematical morphology algorithm. The results demonstrate a sensitivity of 98.75%, specificity of 96.47%, and an overall accuracy of 92.45% for the proposed algorithm. Processing the 35,126 retinal images from the database takes an average time of 12.6 seconds per image. This study highlights the efficacy of employing K-means clustering and Mathematical morphology techniques in developing a robust tool for diabetic retinopathy lesion identification on retinas. The proposed methodology has the potential to serve as a valuable diagnostic tool, reducing errors and speeding up the diagnosis and treatment of ocular diseases.

articleTitle: Visual Vibration Sensor of an Electromechanical System Using a Mach-Zehnder Interferometer
abstract: This article introduces an innovative algorithm to capture and measure vibrations using the principles of the Mach-Zehnder interferometer. The configuration comprises a CCD camera and a vibrating motor, vibrating at a frequency range of 50 to 200 Hz. The results were evaluated from image processing tools. The technique called “phase unwrapping” was used to assess the results of this study. Regarding the experimental results, the evaluation demonstrated the algorithm's accuracy and effectiveness in detecting and measuring vibrations. These findings can be employed to provide vibrational information on the target machine and improve maintenance schedules and operational safety in industrial environments.

articleTitle: High Signal Isolation Dual-mode Diplexer Using Square Loop Resonator with Tuning Stub
abstract: This article introduces a high signal isolation dual-mode diplexer. The diplexer circuit's configuration incorporates two independently designed dual-mode filters, each capable of determining the position of the transmission zero (Tz). When interconnected to form a dual-mode diplexer circuit, it is demonstrated that this configuration exhibits superior isolation values compared to conventional diplexer circuits, particularly when positioned at the specified Tz location. The proposed dual-mode diplexer is designed for frequencies of 1.95 GHz and 2.14 GHz, delivering isolation surpassing 70 dB and insertion losses better than 1.1 dB in both channels.

articleTitle: Development and Evaluation of the Efficiency of a Stainless Steel Electrostatic Outdoor Air Purifier
abstract: The objective of this research is to design and test a stainless-steel air purifier prototype using electrostatic principles for eliminating dust in outdoor areas. The prototype consists of stainless steel and an electrostatic particle precipitator, a high-voltage direct current source, and a control system. air flow This fan system draws sample air into the system through an electrostatic particle collector for particle charging and sedimentation to improve clean air quality. Test the particle sedimentation performance of the prototype using ANSI/ AHAM AC-standard test methods. 1–2015 with an aerosol particle generator inside a test room size 6×6×3 m. A dust measuring device was used inside the test room. The results of the experiment found that the particle sedimentation efficiency value of the prototype air purifier developed by the prototype air purifier developed Particle sedimentation efficiency was achieved in the test time of 120 minute.

articleTitle: Harmonic Elimination of AC Electric Railway Systems Using Shunt Active Power Filters
abstract: This article presents the power quality improvement in an AC electric railway system by harmonic elimination using the shunt active power filter. The shunt active power filter's reference current is calculated using the synchronous detection with Fourier analysis (SDF) method. The fuzzy controller is used to regulate the current of the shunt active power filter. The article also presents a method for designing fuzzy controllers that is simple to calculate and does not require a mathematical model of the system. The Simulink/MATLAB program was used to model the AC electric railway system with harmonic reduction by the shunt active power filter. The results confirmed that the Fuzzy controller created by the proposed method performs better than the PI controller for controlling the compensating current. Moreover, the shunt active power filter can reduce current harmonic in the AC electric railway system. The percentage value of total harmonic distortions (%THD) after compensation of the source currents is decreased and follows the IEEE standard 519–2022.

articleTitle: Computational Study of the Interaction between Alkali Metal Ions and Graphene by $\text{DV}-\mathrm{X}\alpha$ Method
abstract: Aiming to develop negative electrode materials for secondary batteries, we investigated the interaction between Li<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>, Na<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> and K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> alkali metal ions, and graphene using <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{DV}-\mathbf{X}\boldsymbol{\alpha}$</tex> method. The BOP results confirmed that there are weak interactions between alkali metal ions and graphene cluster. The density of states of graphene and alkali metal ions were also calculated with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{DV}-\mathbf{X}\boldsymbol{\alpha}$</tex>. From these results, it was suggested that not only electrostatic interactions, but also the effects of orbital overlap between graphene and alkali metal ions cannot be ignored. Calculations by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{DV}-\mathbf{X}\boldsymbol{\alpha}$</tex> in our study could be completed within a few minutes per structure showing that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{DV-X}\boldsymbol{\alpha}$</tex> is a very practical method in material design. Furthermore, we also investigated a system where a carbon atom in graphene cluster was replaced with a silicon atom, and then calculated the interaction between alkali metal ions and the graphene cluster. We found that it is possible to control the strength of the interaction between alkali metal ions and graphene by adjusting the silicon substitution concentration.

articleTitle: Magnetic Field Simulation of Multiphase Wind Generator Using 3D Finite Element Method
abstract: This paper, a magnetic field mathematical model is presented in a multiphase generator designed with two different stator winding configurations: 3 -phase and 6 -phase, both designs have same specifications in other aspects, including a 6-pole rotor, 36 slots, and double-layer winding. The aim is to analyze and compare the distribution of magnetic field, electric power, and electric current generated by both designs under ideal conditions, using the 3D finite element method. The results of the simulation could be explained that increasing the number of stator winding sets in the generator could increase the radial magnetic field, and tangential magnetic field, also increase the electrical power output of the generator.

articleTitle: LED light bulb brightness adjuster using Buck Converter for vegetables growing
abstract: A system for varying the brightness of LED lights using a buck converter for use in agriculture is presented in this research. The single-phase AC to DC converter circuit regulates the brightness of LED lights. The MOSFET switching can be controlled using a microcontroller to provide a pulse width modulation signal, allowing the AC to DC Converter circuit to power the LED grow light bulb.

articleTitle: Improvement of Renz's Active Band-Pass Filter Using Uniformly Distributed RC Circuit
abstract: This paper presents the improvement of Renz’ s active band-pass filter. We proposed two types of band-pass filter. The first type of filter circuit structure, resembles to Renz's band-pass filter. The circuit comprising a single gain amplifier and three uniformly distributed RC network (URC). The second type band-pass filter circuit configuration consists of a gain amplifier with one URC and a double capacitive layer (DURC). From the experimental results, it is showed that the behavior of the proposed band-pass filter gives good narrow bandwidth, high <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex> and low sensitivities compared to the Renz's filter.

articleTitle: Reducing Electricity Cost in the Setup Process of Pipe Fittings Using ECRS Technical
abstract: This research aimed to reduce electricity costs in the production process. A case study of a pipe fittings company based on actual issues, which were prioritized afterwards by the Pareto diagram that shown excessive energy in EM-12 and LC-44 set up process. It was found that there were problems of wastes from motion and from production process. Therefore, this research suggests guidelines to reduce that electricity cost by finding open area, arranging fixture shelves close to machines to reduce motion distance, and designing appropriate shelves for fixture to reduce wastes in production process. ECRS Technical was applied in operating process. The results indicate a reduction in motion process of 70 meters and setup time in processing process reduced by 68.85 minutes. Therefore, the electricity costs of the motion process are reduced by 36,559.34 baht per year, accounting for 94.80%, and the electricity costs of the processing process are reduced by 97,256.77 baht per year, accounting for 80.07%. So, the total reduction of electricity costs 133,816.11 baht per year. This paper shows that these ECRS techniques reduce the electricity cost and increase the efficiency of energy consumption in the setup process of the Pipe Fittings company.

articleTitle: The PI Control for a Boost Derived Hybrid Converter to Supply DC and AC Loads
abstract: The PI controller designed for a boost derived hybrid converter (BDHC) is proposed in this paper. The DC and AC output voltages can be effectively controlled in both transient and steady states. The parameter gains of the PI controller are calculated using a mathematical model of the simple boost converter. Both DC and AC loads are fed by the desired voltage levels generated by BDHC with the PI controller in voltage and current loops. The simulation results certify that the designed PI controller provides the effective performance of both output voltages in a wide range of operating variations.

articleTitle: Influence of Processes Parameter on the Machinability of Wire Electrical Discharge Machining for Tool Steel Grade JIS SKD 11
abstract: Wire electrical discharge machining is a modern manufacturing process that is widely used on difficult-to-cut materials with a controlled discharge current in order to erode a conductive workpiece. An adjustment of the controlled parameters can possibly effect the machinability of the machining process. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the influence of controlled parameters on the machinability of wire electrical discharge machining for cutting JIS SKD11 grade tool steel. The controlled parameters consist of feed rate and pulse duty factor. The machinability was evaluated in terms of cutting speed and kerf width. In addition the quality of the machined surface was evaluated by arithmetic average roughness. The results showed that cutting speed directly increased with the feed rate for the workpiece at a thickness of 10 mm. However, an approximately 63.50% reduction in the cutting speed was found at the highest feed rate of 5 mm/min and 27.0% for the workpiece thickness at 50 and 25 mm, respectively. The kerf width and surface roughness slightly decreased with the feed rate. The lowest roughness levels were shown at approximately 2.48, 2.40 and 2.46 µm and for the feed rates of 3, 4 and 5 mm/min for the workpiece thickness of 10, 25 and 50 mm, respectively. In addition, the cutting speed, kerf width and roughness of the machined surface increased with the pulse duty factor due to greater duration of pulse on time in the discharge cycle.

articleTitle: A Vision-Based Autonomous AI Tic-Tac-Toe Manipulation System
abstract: For an AI tic-tac-toe manipulator application, a real-time vision-based approach is proposed. The technique employs the RealSense camera to capture color and depth images. Combining object detection and image processing techniques to identify X's and O's positions on the game board. However, we recognize that errors can occur during object movement when using only 2D images. To solve this problem, a calibration method between RealSense and the manipulator based on the point-to-plane ICP algorithm is presented. This method provides the 3D object position in the robot coordinate, resulting in increasing the accuracy from 86.25% to 97.25%. Our experiment shows that this technique is highly effective and can accurately identify position objects.

articleTitle: Thrust Reverser and Air Balance Analysis with a Microcontroller Through a System that Simulates the Rotation of a Jet Engine
abstract: This research project aims to investigate the thrust reverser and air balance analysis using a microcontroller system that simulates the rotation of a jet engine. The study focuses on analyzing the performance and efficiency of the thrust reverser mechanism and the air balance within the engine. By utilizing a microcontroller-based system, real-time data can be collected and analyzed to evaluate the effectiveness of different thrust reverser designs and to optimize air balance for enhanced engine performance. The research methodology includes data collection through simulations and experiments, followed by comprehensive analysis and interpretation of the findings. The results of this study will contribute to the understanding of thrust reverser and air balance systems, providing valuable insights for the design and development of jet engines. From testing the wind speed before opening and after opening the wind barrier door. It can be concluded that the average wind speed before opening the air barrier door was 38.05 kilometers per hour. and after opening the air barrier door Average wind speed is 31.55 kilometers per hour.

articleTitle: Temporal Keyframe Technique based on CNN and LSTM for Enhancing Lip Reading Performance
abstract: The purpose of this research is to present a method for improving lip reading performance through the analysis of temporal keyframes using CNN and LSTM. The performance of the model is determined by employing the input data from the data preparation process. The lip image data is divided into three groups for development: 3 frames, 5 frames, and 10 frames, which include half-lip image data. Lip reading research has never been conducted before based on the assumption of a typical human body shape with left and right symmetry, as in this study. When the unseen test set was evaluated, 10 frames achieved the best recognition rate, with results of 0.879% accuracy for the full lip image dataset and 0.868% accuracy for the half lip image dataset, exhibiting comparable performance.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Trickle Timer under Uncertainty Channel
abstract: In this paper, we present an evaluation of trickle timer algorithms based on the RPL protocol under uncertainty channel. To achieve the objective of the smart grid in which the trickle timer should trick the DIO transmission or suppression appropriately according to the health of low-memory devices such as smart meters. Under uncertainty channel, the existing trickle timer algorithms immediately activate the route maintenance process once the uncertain condition is detected. In practice, the power of noise which encounters the transmission signal may uncertain may vary ranging from 0 to 2 dB. Therefore, the uncertain behavior affects the trickle timers’ process significantly. From the simulation results, the network lifetime and packet delivery ratio (PDR) reduce according to the strength of the uncertainty. Once the energy-aware adaptive trickle timer takes workload and transmission performance into the account, this trickle timer can extend the network lifetime more than the original trickle timer which determines only the transmission performance. On the other hand, EEAT shows packet delivery ratio higher than the original trickle timer.

articleTitle: Fault Type Classification in the Electric Distribution System Integrated Electric Vehicle Charging Demand
abstract: With the growing popularity of electric vehicles (EVs) and the integration of EV charging infrastructure into distribution systems, the need for efficient fault classification techniques has become paramount. This paper proposes a comprehensive approach for fault classifications in distribution systems that incorporate EV charging. To address this challenge, a fault classification algorithm by using differential evolution (DE) was proposed. By considering multiple data sources, including voltage measurements, and current waveforms, the algorithm achieves a high level of accuracy and robustness in fault classification. The results demonstrate its effectiveness in accurately identifying different fault types, including short circuits between line and line-to-ground faults. In conclusion, the proposed algorithm offers an effective solution for the accurate and fastly identification of various fault types, enabling utilities and operators to enhance the reliability and resilience of distribution systems in the context of increasing EV adoption.

articleTitle: Electrical Discharge Machining Process on Tungsten Carbide Using Copper Titanium-Nitride Electrode Materials
abstract: Tungsten carbide, commonly used as a cutting tool, has hard properties. However, being brittle makes the material difficult machining to shape. Therefore, the researcher tested the electrical discharge machining process on tungsten carbide using copper titanium-nitride electrode materials to study the creation of a copper titanium-nitride (Cu-TiN) composite electrode that went through the sintering process. The temperature 1,100 “°C” use a compression force of 180 “MPa” at different mixing ratios. that affects work efficiency in the electrolysis machining process of tungsten carbide, it was found that the copper titanium-nitride (Cu-TiN) electrode with a mixture ratio of Cu 80%, Ni 3%, TiN 17% had the highest hardness value of 100. 76. “HV”. It has the lowest electrical resistance value of 0. 39188 “Ω'cm” that allows electric current to flow through most easily than other mixture ratios. Including copper at a ratio of 1 00% and bonding of the neck growth. The bond between the particles was the best from the SEM test, so the researcher used a mixture ratio of Cu 80%, Ni 3 %, TiN 17% as the electrode in the EDM process on tungsten carbide workpieces. compare with 100% copper alloy electrode, using the efficiency factor by adjusting the current and the control variable values were kept constant in the same experiment of adjusting the on-time and adjusting the off-time. It was found that the MRR material removal rate of tungsten carbide materials among the electrode mixtures of Cu80%, Ni3%, Tin17%, it had the best removal value of 0. 0047 “g/min” and had the lowest surface roughness value on tungsten carbide workpieces at 1.787 “µm”.

articleTitle: Cucumber Disease Identification Using Multiple Machine Learning Classifiers with a Pre-Trained VGG16 Model
abstract: Agriculture is a foundational element of global food security and economic stability, yet it faces the perennial challenge of crop diseases, which can significantly impact yield and quality. Traditional disease detection methods, reliant on manual inspection, are labor-intensive and can lack precision. Addressing this, we propose a hybrid model that combines the strengths of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and machine learning classifiers for the automated detection of diseases in cucumber plants. Specifically, we employ the VGG16 network, renowned for its feature extraction capabilities, coupled with Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), Decision Trees (DT), and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) classifiers. Our model is trained on a dataset consisting of high-resolution cucumber images, with 80% used for training and 20% for validation. Performance metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score are utilized for evaluation, with a particular emphasis on the F1-score for its balance between precision and recall. The SVM classifier emerges as the most effective, followed by RF, KNN, and DT. The results, analyzed through confusion matrices, validate the SVM's superior performance in accurately classifying the health status of cucumber plants. This study not only enhances disease detection accuracy but also suggests a direction for future agricultural practices, highlighting the potential integration of such models into real-time crop management systems.

articleTitle: Applied Depthwise Separable-based Convolutional Neural Network Classification on MobileNet Algorithm for Human Fall Detection
abstract: This paper presents the human fall detection by convolutional neural network (CNN) classification and MobileNet algorithm. In order to reduce the number of parameter, we propose a vision-based fall detection model, that is called “Applied Depthwise separable-based CNN-MobileNet (ACM) algorithm”. This model is based on CNN, deptwise convolution and pointwise convolution of MobileNet algorithm. Experimental results show the accuracy of proposed ACM model about 97.68% and number of parameters of proposed ACM model is less than conventional CNN model.

articleTitle: Improving Input Voltage Transient Response in Voltage Mode Control of DC-DC Boost Converter
abstract: The dc-dc boost converter is commonly utilized to elevate lower input voltages to higher output levels. However, sudden fluctuations in the input power supply can induce line transients, leading to noticeable overshooting and undershooting in the output voltage. These deviations have the potential to inflict damage on downstream equipment and cause operational disruptions. This study focuses on augmenting the transient response to input voltage variations in a dc-dc boost converter that uses voltage mode control. To improve the input voltage transient response, an additional adaptive gain was incorporated into the voltage control loop. Simulation results illustrated that the proposed method effectively minimized both undershoot and overshoot in the output voltage, even when confronted with varying input voltages.

articleTitle: Study on the Slope Diffraction from a Planar Material Junction by Using an Approximate UTD Ray Solution
abstract: This work focuses on studying slope diffraction from the canonical configuration of a planar material junction between two thin materials. Slope diffraction becomes particularly crucial when a null pattern of the source is illuminated onto the discontinuity of the geometry, especially in cases where a source, such as a current moment in the x-direction, is mounted on the material's surface. Therefore, this work aims to investigate the effect of slope diffraction in a planar material junction between two thin materials and present the results when a current moment in the x-direction is mounted on the material surface. It's worth mentioning that numerical differentiation of the first-order diffraction coefficient is employed to compute the slope diffraction coefficient and determine the slope-diffracted fields in this study.

articleTitle: Enhancing Antenna Gain and Radiation Patterns Through the Investigation of Chiral Metamaterials
abstract: The determination of chirality in materials, a crucial parameter in electromagnetic research, is explored in this study. Chirality, as elucidated by Equation 9, hinges on the refractive index <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(n)$</tex>, setting it apart from traditional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> value determination. The investigation necessitates the assessment of both circularly polarized waves, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$CP_{R}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$CP_{L}$</tex>, as opposed to linearly polarized waves, involving the placement of materials in their path. Subsequently, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> values for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$CP_{R}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$CP_{L}$</tex> are ascertained and applied in Equation 9 to compute the chirality of the material. Our research delves into methodologies for extracting epsilon <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\epsilon)$</tex>, mu <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mu)$</tex>, impedance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(z)$</tex>, and refractive index <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(n)$</tex>, culminating in the development of a program for their computation via S-Parameters, fundamental data stemming from simulations or measurements. The program's practical utility is demonstrated through validation with air, yielding results congruent with air's inherent properties. This substantiates the program's efficacy in accurately determining diverse material properties.

articleTitle: Electronically Tunable High Pass Filter-Based MSO Employing VD-DIBAs
abstract: This research presents the VD-DIBA as a voltage-mode MSO. First-order high-pass filters, consisting of a grounded capacitor, two resistors, and a VD-DIBA per phase, are cascaded in the suggested MSOs design. MSOs with a 120-degree phase difference can be produced with this arrangement. Notably, independent electronic tuning of the oscillation state and frequency is possible. Through the use in PSPICE program simulations, the oscillation's frequency and conditions are verified, offering empirical support for the suggested theoretical framework.

articleTitle: Magnetic Fields Simulation of Underground Power Transmission Lines Multiple Systems using 3-D FEM
abstract: The characterization of magnetic field intensity generated by underground cables, along with detailed modeling to unveil its true nature, remains a significant challenge. To address this, our paper proposes a mathematical model for diagnosing the magnetic field intensity of 22 kV and 115 kV underground power lines using the 3D finite element method to simulate the magnetic field. Considering both 22 kV and 115 kV underground cables, the 3D model, employing the proposed finite element method, is based on the linear partial differential equation method, incorporating weighted residuals and the Galerkin method. These cables will be arranged in different configurations, and the experimental results will be compared with magnetic field values to understand their mutual effects. Additionally, a comparative analysis will assess the impact of magnetic field values on humans and electrical equipment, comparing them against the ICNIRP standard. The study involves an examination of the magnetic fields of several underground transmission lines using the 3D finite element method. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method can graphically depict the 3D distribution of the electromagnetic field around 22 kV and 115 kV underground cables with detailed characteristics. Furthermore, the proposed model is employed to determine the magnetic field distribution at various underground depths. Thus, the proposed method proves capable of revealing the true nature of underground cables and assessing cable arrangements at different depths.

articleTitle: Design and Experimental Verification of an Integrated Boost-Flyback Converter with Voltage Multiplier
abstract: This paper introduces the design and experimental validation of an integrated boost-flyback converter with a voltage multiplier (IBFCVM). It describes the operation of the IBFCVM and provides its essential voltage and current equations. A phototyped circuit design for a 72W, 12V-to-120V IBFCVM is presented. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed IBFCVM exhibits effective output voltage regulation, achieving an impressive efficiency of 89.9%.

articleTitle: Surface Roughness of Electrical Terminal Blocks in the Plastic Injection Process
abstract: Surface roughness is an indicator of surface quality in the plastic injection industry. Selecting the appropriate conditions is one way to reduce surface roughness. The purpose of this study is to analyze surface roughness by finding factors that affect roughness and finding suitable factors for the plastic injection process of wire harness connector pieces. This experimental design examines the effects of 5 factors affecting surface roughness. In the analysis, the results from examining the surface of the workpiece and images from the laser electron microscope will be used to check for differences in the workpiece and the surface characteristics of the workpiece in the imperfect state of the workpiece and the perfect condition of the workpiece. The results of the study found that appropriate factors have a significant effect on the average surface roughness. The optimum conditions are the parameters: Injection pressure at 110 MPa, holding pressure at 50 MPa, holding time at 0.5 sec, Injection speed at 50 mm/s, and Injection Stroke at 10 mm., making it possible to reduce the roughness of the work surface and the perfect condition of the workpiece

articleTitle: Bag of Tricks Toward Enhanced Shuttlecock Detection from Badminton Videos
abstract: Shuttlecock detection is crucial for video analysis in badminton matches, but identifying tiny and fast-moving shuttlecock from videos is still challenging. In this work, we propose several tricks that can be attached to a state-of-the-art shuttlecock detection algorithm, TrackNetV2. Our proposed tricks include introducing residual network, Leaky ReLU, and post-addition batch normalization, all based on the deep learning theory. The contribution of this work is to apply the well-known techniques to shuttlecock detection successfully, and this is the first attempt in shuttlecock detection literature. Our experiments on a public badminton dataset demonstrate that our proposed tricks can substantially improve TrackNetV2 regarding precision, recall, F1, and accuracy from 84.8%, 81.8<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>,83.3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, and 75.8% to 88.2%, 83.1%,85.3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, and 78.1%, respectively.

articleTitle: Generation Maintenance Scheduling Considering Carbon Tax and Social Cost
abstract: In power systems, generation maintenance scheduling (GMS) is operated to prolong life span of generation units (GUs) to increase the system reliability. Nonetheless, environmental concerns have been widely considered, leading to the social cost and carbon tax policies enforced in several countries. By considering these issues, this paper proposes multi-objective GMS models to minimize the GMS costs incurred by operation and maintenance, social impact, and carbon tax. The models are solved based on the lexicographic method. The GSM algorithm in the published work is also run to demonstrate the robustness of the results. A numerical example is implemented on the IEEE 24-bus test system. The outcomes suggest that the proposed GMS algorithms outperform previous work in terms of financial cost, carbon generation, and system reliability for a generation company.

articleTitle: Study of Class E Inverter for Induction Heating in High Temperature
abstract: This paper investigates the effects of parameter changes on a class E inverter used for heating by induction in applications that require high temperatures. To test, vary the input voltage between 25 and 225 volts. The inverter is accomplished with IGBT switching. The loss of single IGBT switch reduced by switching of the single IGBT switch turn on within zero voltage switch. The frequency at which switching occurs of the inverter can be changed to alter the output power. Throughout the heating process, the testing unit, which has a 5-7 kHz working frequency range and is rated at around 1000W, is evaluated under load-parameter fluctuation. The study delves into single-switch functioning concepts, with simulation and experimental outcomes providing validation.

articleTitle: Dynamic Plasma Treatment in Flowing Water: A Transformative Approach to Wastewater Treatment
abstract: In contrast to conventional static wastewater treatment methods, dynamic water flow plasma treatment is investigated as a potential remedy for industrial wastewater. The study finds the ideal circumstances for effective wastewater treatment by examining the interaction between water kinetics and radicals produced by plasma. In our prototype, the discharge characteristics and plasma treatment effectiveness of tungsten electrodes in a dynamic water prototype are investigated in two stages of research. The ideal current, as indicated by the results, is between 350 and 400 A, indicating efficient sediment formation. Water treatment at flow rates of 2–4 mL/s appears promising, as total dissolved solids, chemical oxygen demand, and biochemical oxygen demand are all significantly reduced. Beyond the confines of academia, this research offers pathway to more effective wastewater treatment solutions for businesses that handle organic pollutants in dynamic water environments.

articleTitle: Differentiating Analysis of Beef, Pork, Bovine Blood, and Porcine Blood via Electronic Olfaction Technology
abstract: The objective of this research is to design an affordable electronic nose (E-nose) system for the identification and discrimination of beef, pork, bovine blood, and porcine blood based on their emitted gases, with a focus on enhancing food safety and quality. The proposed E-nose system comprises two integral components. The first component governs the control of odor direction, flow rate, and detection within the chamber. The second component is responsible for program control and data recording, facilitating subsequent analysis. All E-nose devices are thoughtfully encased within a compact, portable handbag-style enclosure. The gas detection chamber is equipped with a suite of sensors, including those for temperature, humidity, and array gas sensors. The air flow control system is equipped with an air pump and an array of moisture and odor filters. The flow system incorporates two distinct flow paths, regulated through solenoid valve control. Each 50 g sample was tested and rigorously processed through principal component analysis (PCA). The resulting clusters were further grouped using the K-means method in R version 4.2.0. The outcomes of the study conclusively demonstrate the efficacy of the low-cost electronic nose in distinguishing between cattle and pig meat and, notably, the unique olfactory profile of beef, thus underscoring its utility in food analysis and quality assessment.

articleTitle: Numerical Integration Study for Spherical Near-Field to Far-Field Transformations
abstract: This paper presents a numerical integration study for spherical near field (NF) to far field (FF) transformations. The trapezoidal and Simpson 1/3 numerical integration methods are employed in the NF to FF transformations algorithm. The performance of both numerical integrations is investigated. In this study, a seven patch array antenna is employed. Simulated FF results are performed by three dimensional (3D) simulation program (CST Microwave Studio) and used as the reference. The collected NF sampling data is divided into two cases; 1) over-sampled NF angles of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta = \phi = {2^{\circ}}$</tex> and 2) under-sampled NF angles of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta = \phi = {12^{\circ} }$</tex>. The investigation reveals that, in the case of under-sampled near field (NF) angles of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta = \phi = {12^{\circ} }$</tex>, the trapezoidal demonstrates lower errors of the FF radiation pattern in comparison to those of Simpson 1/3. Particularly, the trapezoidal is suitable for the under-sampled NF measurement case.

articleTitle: The Study Boost Single-Phase PFC Converter for Induction Heating Applications
abstract: This paper proposes the application of a power factor correction (PFC) boost converter and a half-bridge resonant inverter for hot tensile testing (HTT), a method for determining the characteristics of materials at elevated temperatures. When the heating temperature exceeds the normal range, computer simulation is used to study and design circuits. The simulation results reveal that the boost converter circuit is effective. It can convert the input current into a sine wave in phase with the input voltage. By using the switch at a frequency of 51 kHz, the half-bridge inverter circuit uses a switching frequency of 46 kHz and can control the DC output voltage from 20 - 340 volts with an input current of 5 amps.

articleTitle: Design of A Rotated 3D-Printed Lens Antenna Assembly with An Ultra-Wideband Antenna for Beam Steering Applications
abstract: The paper presents the rotated 3D-printed dielectric lens assembly with an ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna for use in the beam-steering applications. The focus is on achieving beam steering by combining the rotated 3D-printed dielectric lens assembly with a hemispherical lens and UWB antenna. The UWB antenna is fabricated on an FR-4 substrate, while the hemispherical lens and the rotated 3D-printed lens assembly are made from Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene (ABS). To enable the hemispherical lens to rotate to the specified angle, a set of rotatable 3D-printed lenses was etched to determine five angles: -60degrees, -30degrees, 0degrees, 30degrees, and 60degrees. Both simulation and measurement results indicate that at a beginning frequency of 3.5 GHz, the beam cannot be steered when using the UWB antenna with the 3D-printed ABS lens rotated hemispherical lens assembly. However, at middle and high frequencies of 7.0 GHz and 10.0 GHz, respectively, the beam can be steered according to the direction of rotation of the hemispherical lens.

articleTitle: Open Source Dynamic Simulation Techniques of the Sixth Order Model of Synchronous Machine
abstract: This paper presents the open source dynamic simulation techniques of a synchronous machine for dynamic stability analysis. The model of synchronous machine is based on the sixth-order model. It consists of the differential equations (DE) of speed, rotor angle, transient voltage, and subtransient voltage. The computation of initial conditions and evaluation of dynamic stability of synchronous generator are systematically described in this paper. This method allows us to investigate the dynamic performance of synchronous machine by using computer programming languages such as FORTRAN, C, etc. The proposed method is validated against the method from the closed source software package.

articleTitle: Magnetic GAA (MAG-GAA) for Vertical and Horizontal Magnetic Field Detection
abstract: The Gate All Around (GAA) is introduced as a magnetic sensor to sense the vertical and horizontal magnetic field applied to the device. Magnetic GAA (MAG-GAA) consisting of one source contact, one gate contact wrapped around the channel, and four drain contacts are created and simulated for the two-dimensional magnetic field detection using Sentaurus. The proposed device structure of MAG-GAA is designed and operated based on the current mode of the Hall effect. The vertical magnetic field is sensed by activating the drain contacts D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. To detect the horizontal magnetic field, the drain contacts D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> positioned at the top and bottom surfaces of the device are enabled. The differential drain current is obtained as the magnetic response in both detections. MAG-GAA in which the channel length and width are 10 nm and 5 nm respectively is simulated by applying the magnetic field 0.1 T, 0.2 T, 0.3 T, 0.4 T, and 0.5 T in +z, -z, +y, and -y directions. Their respective magnetic responses are illustrated, and the Hall current reaches the highest value at the magnitude of the magnetic field 0.5 T in both cases of magnetic field detection. The sensitivity of MAG-GAA for vertical magnetic field detection is better than its sensitivity for the horizontal magnetic field.

articleTitle: Waveguide Diplexer Design using MATLAB GUI for Microwave Engineering Education
abstract: This research presents a waveguide diplexer design using the simulator based on the K-inverter technique, which was developed using the GUI function of MATLAB® for microwave engineering education. The bandpass filter was synthesised using the Chebyshev approximation theory to design the structure of the inductive iris and the length between each iris in the waveguide. The diplexer designed using the developed GUI program was implemented in the operating frequency range of 8.35 - 8.65 GHz and 8.85 - 9.15 GHz, optimized performance with the commercial simulator. The simulated results of the designed waveguide diplexer BPF filter using the developed simulator can be designed consistently with the designed BPF theory. The designed waveguide diplexer band-pass filter using the developed GUI program can be implemented and used effectively as a teaching media for learning and teaching in engineering education.

articleTitle: Implementation of Photovoltaic Power Maximization through Dynamic Power and Current Control
abstract: A novel approach to optimizing photovoltaic (PV) power through adaptive step size adjustments based on variations in PV module output power and current is introduced in this research paper. Utilizing the incremental conductance technique, the algorithm dynamically adjusts the duty cycle of a step-up converter, optimizing the operating point of a PV module toward the maximum power point (MPP). By eliminating the need for a multiplier and requiring no preceding knowledge of PV module output characteristics, this approach stands out for its efficiency. Hardware implementation and a comparison with a fixed step-size strategy demonstrated superior tracking speed (52% faster) and impeccable accuracy. The proposed method accelerates the maximum power point tracking (MPPT) process and also significantly enhances the overall performance of the PV system. The study presents a breakthrough promising a more responsive and precise system for optimizing PV power, showcasing potential advancements in renewable energy technology.

articleTitle: Exploring Accurate and Error-Reducing Techniques for Calculating Support and Resistance Prices on Forex Charts
abstract: The provided information details the principles of Support and Resistance (SAR) points, explaining how they manifest as narrow trading ranges, act as reversal and support points in graphs, and how they may expire due to volume depletion. The theory also proposes a hypothesis regarding the quantities associated with SAR points, addressing the impact of buying and selling volumes on graph behavior. Equations are introduced to calculate SAR point quantities and predict graph direction in relation to SAR points. The research emphasizes that SAR points are instrumental in guiding trading decisions and should be considered in investment strategies. Furthermore, the text acknowledges that real-world data often deviates from the theoretical framework due to the presence of noise in Forex price charts, a topic to be explored in future research.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Heart Sound Denoising Using Adaptive Line Enhancer with LMF Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study of heart sound denoising techniques by employing the Adaptive Line Enhancer (ALE) with the Least Mean Fourth (LMF) algorithm. Three variations of the ALE using LMF are developed and evaluated. The first approach replaces the conventional Least Mean Square (LMS) algorithm with LMF in the ALE structure. The second approach adopts a transform domain framework, and a Hadamard domain LMF is developed and used for ALE. Since the transform domain LMF requires the FIR filter order to match the dimension of the transformation, a novel structure of the transform domain ALE is developed, allowing the FIR filter order to be independent of the transform dimension. The study evaluates the performance of the ALE with LMF algorithm in both domains, alongside the proposed new structure. Simulated tests, focusing on steady-state behavior as the key performance index, demonstrate the superior performance of the newly developed transform domain ALE, surpassing both the time domain ALE with LMS and LMF algorithm and the conventional transform domain approach.

articleTitle: Non Voltage Feedback Bluetooth Power Supply
abstract: This paper introduces a voltage regulator circuit for various Bluetooth devices, designed to operate without voltage feedback. The circuit achieves a 5.1% error margin at a 5V(DC) output voltage and employs a minimal number of components, rendering it a practical solution. The results demonstrate a reduction in harmonic noise in the output voltage during operation. Measurement outcomes, featuring a comparison of harmonic signals, are presented using a digital storage oscilloscope (100MHz 2GSa/s).

articleTitle: The Optimum Switching Bilateral of Various Mix Noise Filters to reduce Medical X-Ray Images
abstract: In the past few years, image processing has been widely adopted for symptom diagnosis of medical application. To achieve accurate analysis, the medical applications require high quality image for applying to the symptom diagnosis applications. However, the medical image quality may drop due to the imperfection of devices and the environment. Noise is one of the most critical factors that reduces the image quality where the noise may form by combining two types of noises. In this paper, we considered four well-known mixed noise filters including TF, BM3D, NCSR and OSBF filters. Since the OSBF filter is the alternative version of SBF filter that requires to determine the optimal weights, therefore we first determine the optimal weights for the medical image under the combination of Gaussian noise and salt-and-pepper noise. Then, we evaluate the filtering performance under three metrics including PSNR, SSIM and filtering time. As a result, OSBF filter achieves the best filtering performance since it can reduce the noise effect, preserve image details and consumes the short filtering time. On the other hand, the filtering performance of the TF filter suffers from the combining of salt-and-pepper noise.

articleTitle: Development of Autonomic Docking Algorithm for Autonomous Mobile Robots by Integrated with Behavior Tree
abstract: This paper is to introduce the development of autonomic docking for autonomous mobile robots (AMR) using behavior trees (BT) and gazebo simulation software in a ROS2 environment. The virtual robot in this study is capable of moving around and locating the charging station by using the camera to identify the ARTag on the map generated through simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) data. BT is used to develop an autonomous docking algorithm and compared three different scenarios through experiments with the AMR. In the experiments, the parameters were adjusted when the AMR was positioned 2 m away from the charging station along the x-axis, with no discrepancy along the y-axis. Additionally, the parameters were tweaked when there was a y-axis discrepancy of ± 0.25 m in cases 2 and 3. The results indicated that modifying the heading tolerance can reduce docking errors and improve the efficiency of the algorithm. Moreover, using BT to design algorithms can enhance functionality and simplify the system's operation.

articleTitle: Noise Detection Capability Exploration of Three Variance Principle and Local Stochastic for High Fix Value Impulsive Noise
abstract: In noise extermination association, particularly the fix value impulsive noise (FVIN), the latest noise extermination system, which is conventionally constituted of noise disclosure sub-system and noise replacement sub-system, is an unavoidable preprocess system that must be executed before the other convoluted image systems. As a result, one of the ultramodern noise disclosure sub-system is the Three Variance Principle and Local Stochastic (TVP-LS) that was emanated from median filter (SMF) in order to surpass the deficiency of the precedent noise disclosure sub-system for FVIN in 2019. Accordingly, this philosopher desertion focuses on exploring the noise detection capability based on TVP-LS for all noise distribution of FVIN (10%-90%) in noisy detection rate, noiseless detection rate, miss rate and fault alarm perspective. In the first experimental exploration, large number noisy portraits, which are contained of Girl, Lena and Pepper at for all noise distribution, are examined the noise detection capability based on TVP-LS in order to determine the threshold parameter of the optimized number of extreme intensity pixels for gaining the highest noisy detection rate. In the second experimental exploration, these noisy portraits are examined the noise extermination system based on TVP-LS, which is collated with the precedent noise disclosure sub-system such as SMF, MF and AMF.

Author Keywords: Three Variance Principle and Local Stochastic (TVP-LS)

articleTitle: Analyze and Predicting with Data Mining on Customer Churn Dataset
abstract: In the ever-evolving landscape of machine learning technology, the exploration and advancement of novel models are of paramount importance. This paper delves into the realm of customer churn analysis, leveraging data mining techniques to discern patterns and predict future trends. The study employs three distinct data mining approaches, segregating data into training and testing sets for a comprehensive analysis. Notably, XGBoost emerges as a standout performer, boasting an impressive accuracy of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$97.75\%$</tex>. In stark contrast, Logistic Regression exhibits an accuracy of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$85.91{\%}$</tex>, and the Decision Tree method follows closely with an accuracy of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$86.36{\%}$</tex>. Significantly, this research emphasizes the efficacy of harnessing sophisticated machine learning algorithms, particularly XGBoost, in forecasting customer churn. By doing so, it advocates for the integration of proactive business strategies informed by these predictive insights.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven Approach for Event Detection in Distribution Systems using Micro-PMU Measurements
abstract: This study introduces and validates a First Difference (FD) event detection method for power distribution systems, assessing its performance in both simulated and real-world scenarios. Utilizing the IEEE 13-bus feeder system in a Real Time Digital Simulator (RTDS) and Micro-Phasor Measurement Unit (Micro-PMU) data from a distribution system, the proposed FD method proves effective in identifying events such as voltage variations and power-related measures. Unlike comparative methods dependent on precise bounds, the proposed FD method exhibits adaptability across different window lengths, showcasing consistent performance.

articleTitle: Train Collision Avoidance System by X-Band FMCW Radar and Long Range Camera Image Processing
abstract: Sensor fusion between X-Band radar and long-range Pan-Tilt-Zoom (PTZ) camera for train collision avoidance system is proposed. The method of Constant False Alarm Rate (CF AR) is applied for the radar signal processing to improve the correct result of radar detection. The edge detection and object detection by digital image processing are applied to long range camera system for classification of identity and position of the object. Experiments of obstacle detection by radar and camera are performed. The proposed work will benefit the safety improvement of locomotive transportation application in which its details are presented and discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Dota 2 Viewing: Automated Battle Highlights in Esports Videos
abstract: This research outlines a structured process for automatically generating video highlights from Dota 2, a multiplayer online battle arena (MOBA) game. Dota 2's dynamic battles make determining their duration challenging, often requiring manual intervention. However, the game's API provides developers access to critical in-game information, particularly player deaths, which serve as key indicators of battles. The process unfolds in six steps: capturing competition videos, extracting match details, refining the data to account for in-game time variations and game start times, automatic video trimming with attention to overlap resolution, consolidation of video segments, and, finally, the publication of the highlight video. This approach ensures engaging and concise highlight videos, enhancing the viewer experience.

articleTitle: Automated Surface Cleaning Evaluation Algorithm
abstract: To avoid micro-organisms spreading in hospitals, hand hygiene and hospital environment disinfection and cleaning is considered to prevent the infections. Therefore, CDC provides hand hygiene and surface cleaning evaluation methods to ensure that source of micro-organisms is disposed. Basically, the surface cleaning is evaluated by the cleaning evaluator who identifies the unclean area through the brightness area of fluorescent marker shined by blacklight under a dark room. However, the evaluation errors may occur if the determine surface is barely clean where the fluorescent marker is not completely removed. Moreover, it is very difficult to meet the same evaluation standard if the evaluation is done by human estimation. In addition, it takes long evaluation time via visual evaluation. In this paper, we propose an automated surface cleaning evaluation algorithm that evaluates the surface cleaning automatically by extracting the color image component, blue, which is noticeably bright under the blacklight characteristic. In the experiment, we compare the performance of the proposed algorithm using blue component to other image components. As a result, the proposed algorithm shows the highest accuracy determined by the experienced cleaning evaluator. Moreover, the proposed algorithm shows 4.384 times faster of surface cleaning detection than cleaning evaluator.

articleTitle: Enhancing Portraiture: Analyzing the Gap Between Amateur and Professional Photography to Bridge the Divide for High-Quality Self-Portraits
abstract: In this comprehensive research, we meticulously analyzed a dataset of over 1000 images, encompassing both professional and amateur photography. Our results unveiled a striking contrast in the approach of amateur photographers, who tend to emphasize the facial aspect of their subjects, allocating an average of 16.8% of the frame to the face, as compared to professional photographs where the facial area is constrained to just 15% (Figure 2). Additionally, a profound variance in image brightness became evident, with professional images displaying an average brightness of 150.94, while amateurs produced images with a significantly lower average brightness of 131.20 (Figure 3). Simultaneously, professionals excelled in achieving vibrant and saturated colors, reflecting a higher average color tone across all channels, namely Red (R), Green (G), and Blue (B) (Figure 4), with channel ranges documented as R = (195.68, 214.40), G = (115.33, 133.19), and B = (93.90, 109.43). These findings illuminate the pronounced disparities between amateur and professional photography techniques.

articleTitle: Empirical Evaluation of Machine Learning Techniques for Autism Spectrum Disorder
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a complicated neurological system disorder that has severe effects on a person's spoken communication, logical thinking, and person-to-person interaction. The early symptoms start looking visible at the age of two to four years and the main ground of these symptoms could be hereditary or ecological. Presently, the standardized approach for detecting ASDs is usually very time-consuming and the cost of medical care is extravagant. Therefore, early detection of ASD would be helpful. Machine Learning (ML) algorithms have the required potential to predict the chances of having autism or not, based on the type of dataset provided to it and the kind of algorithms that are effectively applied to it. The focus of this study is on screening data sets and the use of machine learning algorithms, including XGBoost (XGB) (Ensemble Technique), Random Forest Classifier (RFC), Support Vector Classifier (SVC), Logistic Regression (LR), and Artificial Neural Network (ANN). Our aim for this research was to develop a model that shortens the process of identification of ASDs at an early stage. The accuracy and precision scores of 92.2% and 0.88, respectively, indicate that our model has done well. Our research could be extended in developing a large-scale model that contains a large dataset having a variety of attributes and the integration of brain and facial MRI scans could be helpful in identifying ASD.

articleTitle: Negative Pressure Cabinet Air Filter Efficiency Alarm System Using Differential Pressure Sensor
abstract: A negative pressure cabinet is like an air filter that effectively prevents dust. Spread of germs Because of the situation Spread of coronavirus disease (COVID-19), The use of negative pressure cabinets is increasing. As a result, many air filter performance checks are less effective. Therefore, a negative pressure cabinet air filter efficiency notification system has been designed on the Blynk application platform. The front measurement was performed using the SDP810 differential pressure sensor. Behind the air filter, the control operation with microcontroller STM32G030K8 processes the data received from the sensors into differential pressure and temperature values. Take the pressure difference value from the calculated sensor and change the units to wind speed and wind flow rate. It was averaged as a percentage displayed on an OLED screen air filter efficiency alert in 3 levels. When the efficiency of the air filter drops below 50 percent, it Will always notify with red LED bulbs. When the efficiency of the air filter drops below 25 percent

articleTitle: Mango Maturity Classification using VGG16
abstract: Mangoes are mainly cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions. The characteristics of mangoes are sour and sweet taste, pleasant aroma and rich vitamin content of nutrients, making them popular fruits. The work investigated mango ripeness classification using various machine learning classifiers by collecting the images of different stages of mango ripeness and then used them to train a Convolution Neural Network (CNN), MobileNet, ResNet50 and VGG16 classifier. The experimental results showed that the CNN, MobileNet, ResNet50 and VGG16 classifiers achieved the accuracies of 81.30%, 85.11%, 73.66% and 90.08%, respectively. The VGG16 achieved the highest classification accuracy, of which classification accuracies from class 0 to class 5 were 98.85%, 98.85%, 95.80%, 95.80%, 95.42% and 95.42%, respectively.

articleTitle: Smart Home Energy Management Algorithm for TOU-Based Demand Response
abstract: This paper proposes a linear programming (LP) method approach for optimal scheduling of the load of electrical appliances in the residential to respond to time-of-use (TOU) electricity prices at various periods. Appliance scheduling by TOU-based Demand Response (ASTDR) can give electricity consumers a benefit. Appliance loads should be shifted from the high electricity price periods not only to minimize the total electricity cost per day but also to reduce peak load demand by controlling the shiftable loads. The simulation result shows that the proposed method can efficiently reduce electricity costs and also help reduce peak demand from the grid during the peak hour by implementing ASTDR.

articleTitle: Transformable Furniture Design by Geometric Transformations with an Engineering Approach
abstract: This paper propose an innovation design of the transformable furniture module that was based on geometric transformations approach. Meanwhile the aim of this research expect to develop the overall of an automatically of furniture paradigm shift with an engineering design methods. The concept of model design was generated here according with the digital transformation platform to enhance of smart furniture set requirements for approaching to the Thailand 4.0 policy especially for a new facility service platform of smart city. The geometric transformation can specify object modelling operations both for local coordinate system such as modeling coordinates in this paper and a global coordinate system as a worldwide coordinates in the future. With cloud communicating paradigm shift, the new era of the stage of the art infrastructure design of Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) system to enhance the computing resources with a long distance remote control and served them as a service on demand with highly dynamic and flexible transportation system that can be considered as a promising solution with Service Level Agreement (SLA) as fidelity with less waiting time.
