While the fuzzy-proportional plus integral control (F-PI) was modified on fuzzy ladder control scheme for enhancing the PLC ability and utility of the overall performance of the system such as dynamic loading effect management in the real time. The photovoltaic (PV) of solar cell system with the Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) controlled by the Arduino controller was used as the optional design for open space area usage. The simulations results were several tested with the modelling design methodology, while the real prototype module was also several tested in the laboratory room that should be satisfied with design concept. The overall of system performance must be revised again in on-site area for more practical to use and stable.

articleTitle: Calibration based on Polynomial Function for Low-Cost Sensors: A Case Study of Air Purifier Filter
abstract: This paper presents a calibration based on a polynomial function to enhance the accuracy of low-cost sensors (LCS) measuring <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P{{M}_{2.5}}$</tex> concentration levels, with a specific focus on the PMS3003 sensor within the LCS category. To process <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P{{M}_{2.5}}$</tex> concentration data recorded by the PMS3003 LCS, an ESP32-based NodeMCU microcontroller is employed. Our approach utilizes polynomial functions for calibrating the PMS3003 LCS, aiming to enhance its accuracy and reliability. The results highlight significant enhancements in accuracy across diverse <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P{{M}_{2.5}}$</tex> concentration ranges. For low (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P{{M}_{2.5}}\ \le$</tex> 200 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu g/{{m}^3}$</tex>), medium (200 < <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P{{M}_{2.5}} \le$</tex> 400 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu g/{{\mathrm{m}}^3}$</tex>), and high (400< <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P{{M}_{2.5}} \le$</tex> 600 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu g/{{\mathrm{m}}^3}$</tex>) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P{{M}_{2.5}}$</tex> concentrations, the proposed method demonstrates a maximum error percentage lower than that of the traditional method: approximately 2%, 5.47%, and 6.92%, respectively. Furthermore, we validate the effectiveness of our calibrated PMS3003 LCS by comparing its measurements with those of a reference device (RD)—the air purifier filter. Overall, the results demonstrate substantial accuracy improvements across varying <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P{{M}_{2.5}}$</tex> concentration ranges.

articleTitle: Improved Modified Plain Gradient Adaptive IIR Notch Filter for Frequency Estimation
abstract: This paper presents an improved modified plain gradient (IMPG) algorithm for a second-order adaptive IIR notch filter (ANF) for frequency estimation. An error function of MPG is modified by squaring before taking the derivative. By using this technique, the initial value-setting problem of MPG is overcome. Computer simulations are drawn to support the claim.

articleTitle: An Induction Heater Using Half Bridge Resonant Inverter for Coffee Bean Roaster
abstract: This article aims to investigate a rotary coffee roaster's induction heating technology utilizing a half-bridge inverter circuit. It operates at 37 kHz, above the resonance frequency, and consumes 1 kW of electricity. According to experiments, it can reach a maximum temperature of 308°C in 10 minutes. After roasting for 13 minutes at the highest temperature of 240 °C, the roasted coffee's physical qualities showed the highest values in the test.

articleTitle: Non-Invasive Egg Monitoring Using Machine Vision Technology for Distinguishing Fertilized and Untilized Eggs
abstract: This study proposes a non-destructive method of measuring fertilized and non-fertilized eggs during the incubation process, using a machine vision system. The experiment involved 28 Rhode Island Red eggs, which were incubated in a basic incubator consisting of a heating and humidity chamber with automated temperature control. The study employed a machine vision system to measure the length and width of eggs and to monitor the incubation process by capturing daily images of the eggs from the beginning of incubation until hatching. Throughout the incubation period, egg weights and photographs were meticulously documented on a daily basis. The egg samples had an average length of 5.42 cm and an average width of 4.16 cm. Furthermore, on the first day of testing, the egg samples had an average weight of 54.06 g, an average volume of 49.24 µm³, and an average density of 1098.71 kg/m³. The study's findings showed a linear decrease in both egg weight and density as the days of incubation increased, for both fertilized and unfertilized eggs. Additionally, the machine vision system developed for this study can accurately track and measure fertilized eggs by analyzing the increased number of blood vessels within the egg. The fertilized eggs display a rapid increase in the number of blood vessels between days 3 and 7. Beyond day 7, the blood vessels area in the binary image of fertilized and hatchable eggs surpasses 200,000 pixels. Of the 26 eggs that hatched by day 21, only 7 successfully developed into chicks, resulting in a success rate of 27%. Starting from the fifth day of incubation, this approach can be utilized for non-destructive detection, allowing for differentiation between fertilized and unfertilized eggs.

articleTitle: Implementing Dual-Inverted L-Shape Grooves on the Dual-Band Monopole Antenna for Portable WiFi, WiMAX, and 5G Applications
abstract: This article studies the utilization of dual-inverted L-shape grooves on a dual-band monopole antenna to enhance portable WiFi, WiMAX, and 5G capabilities. A monopole antenna design includes a rectangular stub with two inverted L-shaped grooves, allowing it to operate at two different frequencies simultaneously. During the process of creating the grooves on the rectangular stub, it was observed that the antenna structure resembles a T-shaped stub positioned on top of a U-shaped stub. The T-shaped stub is responsible for the antenna's low-frequency response at around 2.45GHz and 3.5GHz, whilst the U-shaped stub is used for impedance matching and provides at a frequency of 5.25GHz. Subsequently, the proposed antenna will be fabricated and evaluated, exhibiting an impedance characteristic of around 50.25% and 6.84% for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert \mathrm{S}_{11}\vert$</tex> at frequencies of 3.04GHz and 5.25GHz, respectively. It is important to note that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert \mathrm{S}_{11}\vert$</tex> remains below -10 dB over the whole operational frequency range. Moreover, the antenna shows a gain of roughly 2.18 dB, 3.31 dBi and 2 dB at frequencies of 2.45GHz, 3.5GHz, and 5.25GHz, respectively. Additionally, the suggested antenna exhibits an omnidirectional. In addition, the proposed antenna possesses dimensions in both portable WiFi, WiMAX, and 5G networks.

articleTitle: An Automatic U-turn Machine System Module using Stepper Motor and PLC on Cloud Control
abstract: This paper propose an innovation design of an automatic U-turn machine module in the smart city. The digital platform with the smart electronic circuits design perform the paradigm shift of public automation facilities especially for car management system for reducing the number of traffic accidents when reversing or U-turn. The geometric transformation can specify object modelling operations both for local coordinate system such as modeling coordinates in this paper and a global coordinate system as a world coordinates in the future. With cloud communicating paradigm shift, the new era of the stage of the art infrastructure design of Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) system to enhance the computing resources with a long distance remote control and served them as a service on demand with highly dynamic and flexible transportation system that can be considered as a promising solution with Service Level Agreement (SLA) as fidelity with less waiting time. While an intelligent fuzzy control method on PLC called as fuzzy ladder scheme can enhance the PLC ability and utility of the overall performance of the system such as dynamic loading effect in real time. The photovoltaic (PV) of solar cell system with the Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) controlled by the Arduino controller was used as the battery charging process design as optional usage. The simulations results were several tested with the modelling design methodology, while the real prototype module was also several tested in the laboratory room that should be satisfied with design concept. The overall of system performance must be revised again in on-site area for more practical to use and stable.

articleTitle: Enhancing Trading Strategies Through Multi-MA Analysis: A Comprehensive Study on Trend Identification Techniques
abstract: The research findings reveal the potential profitability of the trading strategy across diverse market conditions. The strategy demonstrates an average annual profit of around 25%, accompanied by a drawdown of approximately 8%, and an impressive win rate of about 80%. Nevertheless, it is important to note that these results may vary based on the specific operational parameters and the choice of financial instruments employed. The study's empirical analysis involved the testing of the strategy using currency pairs, with a primary focus on EURUSD.

articleTitle: The Harmonic Mitigation for Heavy Rail Systems Using Shunt Active Power Filter
abstract: Harmonic distortion has been a significant issue in heavy rail systems. The electric trains act as a nonlinear load to generate harmonic current in the power distribution systems, and it has effects on the power distribution grids, such as increasing power losses of transmission lines and power transformers, interference in the electric railway signaling systems, electromagnetic interference of electric devices, malfunctions of the devices, protective device failures, and short-life electric devices. Therefore, this paper proposes a shunt active power filter for harmonic mitigation in heavy rail systems. For harmonic detection and reference current calculation of a shunt active power filter, this paper employs instantaneous power theory with the Fourier method. Furthermore, compensating current and DC bus voltage controls are also accomplished with PI controllers. The results indicate that the proposed control topology for a shunt active power filter can provide good performance in harmonic mitigation in heavy rail systems. Moreover, the total harmonic distortion of the source current after compensation follows IEEE standard 519–2014.

articleTitle: Novel Bandpass and Periodic Frequency Responses in Non-Metallic Dielectric Metamaterials
abstract: This study explores the remarkable properties of the Box-Ball Structure (BBS) within the 1GHz to 50GHz frequency range. The BBS structure demonstrates consistent bandpass frequencies with a periodic response and maintains a uniform 2.058GHz bandwidth at S11 = -6dB. Unlike metal-based structures, where changing C and L values can lead to frequency-dependent responses, the dielectric BBS structure exhibits stability. Its dielectric properties, including epsilon, mu, and refractive index (n), remain largely unaffected by frequency variations. Furthermore, the BBS structure is found to induce capacitance (C), as per the principles of virtual circuit theory, making it suitable for band-pass filter applications. The liquid state of epoxy resin allows for versatile structural designs, such as a hollow cylinder for omnidirectional antenna signal filtration. This research introduces the BBS as a dielectric resonator with unique properties and potential applications in various industries, particularly in the mobile phone sector.

articleTitle: The Monitoring and Controlling of Wireless Communication with PLC via Internet Access
abstract: This research paper presents a novel system for the Programmable Logic Controller Programming Interface (PLC), which enables wireless control of industrial process systems through a web application using the ESP-WROOM-32S Wi-Fi microcontroller and Siemens PLC SIMATIC S7-1200 CPU 1215 DC/DC/DC (6ES7215-1AG40-0XB0). The system is designed to facilitate programming in both microcontrollers and industrial process systems, with the ladder command used to control the PLC and create a display page and user work orders. The system architecture involves the ESP-WROOM-32S Wi-Fi receiving commands and transmitting data wirelessly via web applications to the PLC, which processes the data and sends it to the appropriate industrial processes. A graphical display page is generated using the Arduino IDE and HTML commands written in C/C++ with HTML to create a user-friendly interface. To measure the operation of industrial process systems, sensors are employed, and a built-in graphic display is included to ease the operation of the systems. This system offers an effective solution for wireless control of industrial process systems with a user-friendly web interface. The combination of the ESP-WROOM-32S Wi-Fi and Siemens PLC S7-1200 ensures reliable and efficient data transmission, which is critical for the effective operation of industrial process systems. Setting up Node-red to work on the Raspberry Pi requires a good understanding of the Linux system used. The PLC must be set up to open the connection ports to install it on the Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+. Programming on Node-red may also require the installation of additional libraries. Despite these challenges, Node-red offers a variety of styles to choose from in controlling and displaying graphical results.

articleTitle: The Fault Detection Method Based on Fuzzy Logic for Boost Converters
abstract: The reliability of the converter system is often reduced by power switch failures. Therefore, converter systems currently need fast switch fault detection and precise switch identification. The approach for the fault detection method for a boost converter based on fuzzy logic, suffering an open-circuit switch fault. The suggested fault detection technique considers the converter behavior investigation, especially the input current slope, when operating in both healthy and faulty states. Moreover, the fuzzy controller is applied to boost converter, which is supplied by a renewable energy source. The simulated results are presented in order to demonstrate the reliability of the suggested fault detection technique under various scenarios.

articleTitle: Parallel Class-E Resonant Inverters with a Common EMI Filter for Domestic Induction Cooker
abstract: This study proposes a method to parallelly connect 2 Class-E resonant inverters for domestic induction cookers. The setup consists of induction heating systems, which include a full-wave rectifier, an electromagnetic interference filter, 2 Class-E resonant inverters, and induction loads connected to each inverter. A PWM control circuit, which enables zero voltage switching (ZVS) and zero voltage and current switching (ZVDS). The aim of using this circuit is to produce a medium-frequency current that passes through the induction coil, thus causing the vessel to heat up through induction heating. Using a common electromagnetic interference (EMI) filter and pulse-width modulation (PWM) control circuit, this study shows a new way to reduce the functioning of systems. This paper provides instructions for constructing important parameters using a Class-E resonant inverter to minimize system complexity. This methodology provides a more pragmatic answer than conventional methods. Both inverters operated with a root mean square (RMS) voltage of 220 V, a frequency of 50 Hz, and an inverter power output of 1,500 W.

articleTitle: Thai-English Name Matching Using Google Translation and Thai Romanization
abstract: Businesses or contracts with illegal persons or persons on sanctions lists are not tolerated by companies. Sanctions lists are used to combat international terrorism by depriving individuals, organizations and institutions associated with terrorist activities of funds and economic resources. Sanctions lists, which can be purchased or sourced, may not contain complete information. Some lists or parts of the lists contain only first and last names in English. Neither first and last names in Thai nor identification numbers are presented. In order to improve the possibility of finding Thai people in a sanctions list, the method of converting Thai first and last names to those in English together with searching a criterion was proposed. Thai transliteration systems, Google Translate (GT), and our proposed methods were studied to convert Thai first and last names, and the results were evaluated using Levenshtein distance, accuracy, and similarity. When applying the royin engine, thai2rom engine, GT and our proposed method, the average Levenshtein distances per first and last name were 6.273, 3.717, 2.308 and 2.157, respectively. To search an English sanctions list, the minimum distance between the thai2rom engine and the GT results can be used as a criterion. It was found that the average distance reduced to 1.981, showing more efficient method to find unfavourable persons.

articleTitle: Automated Counting of Giant River Prawn Larvae using Machine Vision
abstract: In this scholarly endeavor, we introduce a machine vision system tailored for counting giant river prawn larvae within a water-filled vessel. Our system exhibits the capacity to perform real-time and image-based counting of these organisms at a density of 500 individuals per image, achieving an accuracy exceeding 99.40%. This system offers a multitude of distinct advantages over conventional counting methodologies, including rapid processing, high precision, and reduced labor demands. Furthermore, it stands as a non-invasive, non-destructive, and cost-effective solution for counting, thus promising significant improvements in the field of giant river prawn aquaculture.

articleTitle: A Compact Inverted C Patch On-body Antenna for Biomedical Applications
abstract: This paper proposes the design of a compact inverted C patch on-body antenna for biomedical applications. The antenna structure consists of an inverted C patch on the top of the FR4 substrate, integrated with the radiation rectangular patch at the bottom by using a shorted pin. The ground plane is also at the bottom of the FR4 substrate, separated by a gap. The proposed antenna is considered on the human skin in the environment of on-body communications. From simulated results, the antenna has |<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{11}$</tex>| less than -10 dB covered the frequency range of 2.36-2.58 GHz, uni-directional radiation pattern, and -4.5 dBi of gain at 2.45 GHz. It is found that the lossy human skin affects antenna characteristics by reducing its gain and efficiency. Moreover, the proposed antenna is appropriate for on-body communication systems.

articleTitle: Automated Stomatal Detection and Enumeration Using Machine Vision Techniques
abstract: Stomata represent pivotal sites for water exchange in plants, orchestrating the vital processes of gas exchange, photosynthesis, and transpiration. Guarded by specialized cells, stomata regulate the rate of transpiration by opening and closing. The status of stomata, whether open or closed, serves as an indicator of a plant's health. Consequently, the quantification of stomata assumes great significance in scientific research, facilitating the study of stomatal dynamics, density, and distribution on leaf surfaces through diverse sampling methodologies. Both manual stomatal observation and automated detection techniques play crucial roles in this pursuit, impacting fields such as taxonomy, biology, physiology, and eco-physiology. In this study, we have designed a machine vision system utilizing an affordable USB microscope to accurately count stomata on live leaves of the Oyster plant (Tradescantia spathacea Stearn). Functional tests of the developed system reveal its capability to swiftly and precisely enumerate stomata in real-time, achieving an accuracy rate of 68.75%. This innovative approach offers several advantages over conventional counting methods, including increased speed, reduced labor demands, cost-effectiveness, and the capacity to count stomata continuously and in large quantities over extended durations. The developed system empowers scientists with a high-speed, accurate, and efficient means of obtaining stomata count data, while also serving as an educational tool for elementary and secondary students to explore plant morphology and various objects in diverse forms.

articleTitle: An Evaluation of ANFIS Controller for Photovoltaic MPPT using Zeta Converter
abstract: This research presents the performance of the maximum power tracking using the ANFIS algorithm technique on a zeta converter circuit. The researchers used a 285 W monocrystalline PV panel in the research method. This research uses an appropriate design of the Zeta circuit's parameters by selecting a load size of 4.312 ohms. The conditions in solar irradiation (G) based on the highest average light intensity in Thailand at 858 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> used in the experiment at 100%, 75%, 50%, and 25% are 858 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, 637.5 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, 429.0 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and 214.5 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, respectively, and the temperature (T) is set at 40°C based on an average temperature in Thailand. The results show that the output power decreases when the solar irradiation decreases, following a sequential pattern. Comparing the power obtained from PV panels with MPPT and without MPPT shows that the power values were similar at a high rate of solar irradiation. However, at a low rate of solar irradiation, the power values obtained from the solar photovoltaic (PV) panels integrated with the MPPT can produce a higher electrical energy output than without the MPPT installation. Furthermore, this research compares the performance of the MPPT system, which is controlled by a fuzzy logic algorithm and ANFIS. The efficiency values of the circuits are 95.98% and 97.54%, respectively. It can be concluded that the intelligent and swift operation of the ANFIS control obtains higher efficiency than an operation using fuzzy logic control.

articleTitle: Analyzing S-Parameter Variations in Metamaterials: The Impact of Varying Incident Angles for Electromagnetic Waves
abstract: The study investigates how changing the incident angle (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta$</tex>) of electromagnetic waves impacts the structure's frequency response. When <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta$</tex> exceeds 45 degrees, the structure exhibits a heightened sensitivity to the 2nd harmonic, diminishing the 1st harmonic's amplitude. Notably, the 2nd harmonic disappears entirely at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta= 90$</tex> degrees. Within the 0 to 45-degree range, the response aligns with the 1st harmonic. However, the center frequency remains sensitive to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta$</tex>, increasing as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta$</tex> rises. Figures 7 to 12 illustrate these effects, revealing that altering the incident angle of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta$</tex> waves not only shifts the center frequency but also induces changes in the metamaterial properties, impacting its characteristics.

articleTitle: Determining Banana Ripeness Using MobileNet
abstract: Bananas are one of the most popular and economically important fruit crops in the world. Not only do they have a sweet taste, but they are also rich in various nutrients that are useful for human body. To find an efficient method for classifying banana ripeness, images of bananas were used to train the MobileNet, ResNet50, and Convolution Neural Network (CNN) machine learning classifiers. These machine learning classifiers can automatically extract the features from the trained images and then use them to build models for classification. The results indicated that the MobileNet, ResNet50 and CNN classifiers could obtain the accuracies of 98.43%, 94.19% and 95.35%, respectively. The accuracies of MobileNet classification from class 0 to class 6 were 99.62%, 98.85%, 99.23%, 100%, 100%, 99.62% and 99.62%, respectively.

articleTitle: The Memristor's with Microcontroller and Digital to Analog Converter Module MCP4725
abstract: The memristor is the fourth passive electrical device presented in 1971, that is a bipolar circuit device as the relationship between magnetic field-charge matching, based on the four parameters current, voltage, charge, and magnetic field. Memristor emulators are developed in analog digital and microcontrollers, that based on a microcontroller and an analog-to-digital converter. This paper presented the memristor with a microcontroller and digital-to-analog converter module MCP4725. The memristor with the Arduino NANO microcontroller receives a sine wave signal from the function generator via the 10-bit ADC port, then processes the output values through the 12-bit DAC MPC4725 Module using a 5 KΩ resistor load. The results of the experiment found that a memristor can be simulated using phase ship and dead band principles from the microcontroller.

articleTitle: Monitoring Respiration Activity with Bulk Conductivity in a 16-electrode Configuration
abstract: Respiration monitoring is a method for diagnosing the health of the lungs. Current imaging such as CT and MRI still have a limitation of low temporal resolution that could be difficult to be used as monitoring devices. Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT) is an imaging technique with good temporal resolution, but it still requires substantial reconstruction time while the artifacts are usually observable in the images. In this study, bulk conductivity was used to monitor the respiration activity, instead of monitoring based on the reconstruction images. The boundary voltage information that was for EIT image reconstruction was now used for the bulk conductivity estimation. Experimental results on a subject's chest found that the bulk conductivity can efficiently represent the respiration activity. It was consistent with the change that appeared in the reconstruction images and had a very high correlation with the voltage measurement with a -0.98 correlation coefficient.

articleTitle: Implementation of Cloud Computing and Internet of Things (IoT) by Performance Evaluation
abstract: The integration of cloud computing and the Internet of Things (IoT) holds transformative potential across diverse industries. Performance assessment is essential to gauge the quality and efficiency of cloud computing and IoT systems. This paper presents a comprehensive performance evaluation of cloud computing and IoT systems, focusing on three major platforms: Amazon Web Services (AWS), Google Cloud Platform (GCP), and Microsoft Azure. Experimental results encompass various scenarios, including normal operation, heavy load conditions, IoT applications, and scalability testing. The outcomes reveal distinct performance metrics such as response time, throughput, latency, and reliability for each cloud platform.

articleTitle: Improved Neural Network Predictions with Correlation-Based Subset Selection
abstract: This paper introduces a method called Artificial Neural Network with Best Subset Selection (ANNBS) to improve the accuracy of predictions in neural networks. The method involves selecting an optimum subset of variables. Although neural networks have great prediction capabilities, they do not possess inherent processes for selecting variables. This approach uses neural networks to choose variables, employing a Monte Carlo algorithm to conduct subset searching across 1,000 iterations. The analysis encompasses both actual and simulated datasets obtained from neural network models, with correlation coefficients ranging from 0 to 0.8. The correlation coefficient is used as the primary criterion for selecting the optimal subgroup. This strategy is compared to linear regression, traditional neural networks, a hybrid model that combines stepwise regression analysis with artificial neural networks, and model averaging strategies that use information criteria and fit-based weights. The findings indicate that the ANNBS approach consistently delivers low root mean square errors (RMSEs) for both the training and test data, even when the sample sizes are small. As the number of samples increases, the disparity between the RMSEs of the training and test data decreases.

articleTitle: Selective Aggregation of Deep Convolutional Features for Archeological Artifact Retreival
abstract: The increasing availability of digital archaeological image collections has requested the need for advanced techniques in efficiently retrieving and analyzing artefacts. This research introduces a novel retrieval model designed to enhance the retrieval of archeological artefacts from large image databases. The proposed model leverages the hierarchical representations of pyramid features, capturing local and global visual information and then employs to selectively aggregate informative features for generating image embeddings. This not only enhances the discriminative power of the image descriptor but also facilitates the retrieval of artefacts across diverse scales and viewpoints. To capture both visual and semantic aspects, the network is trained by incorporating information related to cultures and time periods using a triplet-based algorithm. Experimental validation conducted on a dataset of historical artefacts from Thailand demonstrates the feasibility of the feature aggregation method, achieving a mean average precision of 80%, which is a significant improvement over existing deep learning-based image retrieval models.

articleTitle: Oscillation Source Identification Using Dissipating Energy Flow in Northeastern Thailand Power Grid
abstract: Power grid oscillation with poorly damped performance is of growing concern. The oscillation source needs to be quickly and precisely identified in order to mitigate the oscillation issues to prevent any detrimental conditions that may arise. An incoming of synchrophasor technology enables the use of dissipating energy flow (DEF) method to practically identify the oscillation source. This paper aims at validating the DEF-based method and then developing an application tool to identify the oscillation source in a practical power grid. The DEF method was validated through various simulated oscillation cases based on IEEE 39-bus system leading to a promising outcome. The DEF-based application for oscillation source identification was developed using Python program and then practically implemented to Northeastern Thailand power grid. The results obtained using the DEF-based application to evaluate actual oscillation events was compared against with those obtained using the commercial software already installed in the system. It can be concluded that the developed DEF-based application offers better precision in capturing oscillation frequency as well as in identifying the oscillation source.

articleTitle: Effect of Class Weights on Imbalanced Classes in Bi-directional LSTM Training for Sleep Apnea Classification
abstract: Sleep apnea, which is defined as the repetitive cessations of breathing during sleep, is the common disorder worldwide. The cost and the process of sleep test to obtain the polysomnogram is not optimal for sleep apnea screening in the large population. A deep learning model was developed to classify the normal and apnea events in a single time-series signal exported from the US National Institute of Health (NIH) sponsored database. Our challenge was to train the model with imbalanced dataset between normal and abnormal respiratory events. Three different methods, Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE), Random Under-Sampling (RUS), and the Class Weights (CW) were chosen to improve the model performance over the original data on five selected signals from polysomnographic dataset. The binary classification outputs were evaluated by four metrics. Our results showed (1) Matthews Correlation Coefficient was highest (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$MCC= 0.1385$</tex>) in the Class Weights method on the nasal airflow signal. (2) Cohen's Kappa score, was highest (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k= 0.0819$</tex>) in SMOTE technique on the abdominal signal, followed by the Class Weights method on the abdominal signal (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k= 0.0687$</tex>) and RUS technique on nasal airflow signal (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k= 0.0441$</tex>). (3) F1-score was highest (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F1= 11.89\%$</tex>) in SMOTE technique on the abdominal signal, followed by the Class Weights method on nasal airflow signal (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F1 = 11.17\%$</tex>) and RUS technique on nasal airflow signal (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F1= 9.16\%$</tex>). The findings suggest that the Class Weights method on nasal airflow and the Class Weights method on abdominal signal were the two combinations to be used in the DL model.

articleTitle: The Fabrication of the Electrospun Polyvinylidene Fluoride (PVDF) Hollow Structure Fibre for Energy Harvesting Applications
abstract: In order to develop ferro electret material, this research aims to produce and investigate energy harvesting performance from a hollow structure polymers using a one-step hollow electro spinning technique. In this study, PVDF (Polyvinylidene fluoride) is used to represent the polar polymer. The obtained hollow and solid structure were characterised in terms of their structural and electromechanical characteristics. The design of the experiment method for producing a hollow fibre structure through electro spinning is discussed in this paper. An SEM (scanning electron microscope) was used to characterise the geometry of the obtained fibres. The geometrical results from the SEM images demonstrate a partial hollow structure for the PVDF electro spun fibres. The partial hollow structure PVDF fibre showed a diameter of around 2 microns. FTIR (Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy) was used to characterise the structural and chemical bonding of the fibres. The FTIR spectra reveal the piezoelectric p-phase in the solid and partially hollow PVDF samples. This agreed with the dominant peak observed from the XRD (X-ray diffractometry) analysis results. In this study, it can be concluded that electro spinning is an effective technique to induce the piezoelectric p-phase of PVDF. The electromechanical characteristics were studied for the solid and partial hollow structure fibres for the PVDF. A tapping test was used to check the obtained samples. The maximum output voltage from the solid PVDF, and partial hollow PVDF were at 6.4 and 8.7 V, respectively. The power density from the solid and partial hollow PVDF electro spun fibre was found at 1.60 and 2.18 mW/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, respectively. The maximum absolute value piezoelectric coefficient for the PVDF hollow fibre group was 28.7 pC/N.

articleTitle: Unleashing Hidden Business Insights: Harnessing Unstructured Big Data through Text Analysis, NLP, and Visualizations for Budgetary Decisions in Governmental Organizations
abstract: Processing Thai language texts can be a challenge due to the complexities of the language, particularly texts from social media and online platforms. This paper introduces an analysis and visualization framework specifically designed to tackle the intricacies associated with processing the Thai language data within the context of online textual content, by utilizing natural language processing (NLP) and visualization techniques. The objectives of this study were to develop an effective Thai text data analysis and visualization framework that allows us to effectively and automatically get a better understanding of the content embedded in Thai textual data. The methodology initiated with a review of existing analysis frameworks and visualization techniques with a specific focus on Thai. The data collection phase encompassed a diverse corpus of Thai text data gathered from online sources. The selected data underwent preprocessing to address language-specific challenges. The proposed Thai analysis and visualization framework consists of multiple stages. Each stage is tailored to accommodate the intricacies of the Thai language, facilitating improved information extraction and text comprehension. The proposed visualization techniques utilize interactive graphs, such as bar charts, line charts, pie charts and donut charts, to offer intuitive and insightful representations of the processed data. Results from our case study show the effectiveness of our Thai analysis framework and visualization techniques in capturing crucial information from online contents written in Thai from governmental organizations.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Growth of Very Small Power Producers (VSPP) and Energy Demand Prediction in Thailand
abstract: This study explores the crucial field of energy consumption projections in Thailand, a country now facing an increase in energy demand. By utilizing machine and deep learning models, we make use of a comprehensive dataset obtained from the official Thailand Energy information website. This dataset has historical data ranging from 1986 to 2022. The focus of our study is around the Neural Network (NN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Linear Regression (LR) models, as well as the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model, which will be used for comparative evaluation. The findings emphasize that the LSTM model outperforms other models, demonstrating the lowest values for Mean Squared Error (MSE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and Mean Absolute Error (MAE). Additionally, the LSTM model achieves a flawless R-squared (R2) score, indicating excellent accuracy in predicting outcomes. In contrast, the LR and SVM models demonstrate satisfactory performance, as evidenced by its low Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), suggesting its applicability for targeted prediction applications. The neural network model demonstrates comparatively higher error rates, suggesting limitations in its effectiveness. The examination of energy data patterns, which includes the aspects of production, distribution, and consumption, provides significant and insightful information for key players in Thailand's energy industry. This analysis emphasizes the importance of accurate energy consumption predictions due to the ongoing increase in demand. This study enhances the comprehension of machine learning implementations in the energy sector of Thailand and underscores the need of choosing the optimal model to ensure precise estimates of energy consumption.

articleTitle: Models of Virtual Battery Systems and Electric Grid Networks to Support a National Energy Trading Platform and Prosumer Integration
abstract: This article's purpose aligns with the Thai government's policy to enhance the power quality and stability of the electricity production and utility distribution systems. Such improvements are essential to boost investor confidence and better serve the country's citizens. This undertaking complements the increasing incorporation of renewable energy sources and the integration of prosumers into the electrical grid as part of Distributed Generation (DG). These efforts are in line with the state's objective to achieve 25% renewable energy usage of the total energy consumption by 2024 and are connected to the National Energy Trading Platform (NETP), which is focused on preparing the electrical distribution system to accommodate the whole system. In response to these developments, this article presents a strategic approach for the distribution utility system to develop electrical grid networks and virtual battery systems. These innovations support a centralized energy trading platform and facilitate the integration of prosumers. The approach combines the planning and management of electrical grid networks with the operational strategies of virtual battery storage systems (VBSS). The benefits of this initiative extend beyond immediate improvements; they equip electrical utility with the necessary knowledge and tools to enhance and control its future electrical distribution systems and to stay adaptive amidst disruptive changes in the energy business model and market.

articleTitle: Data Analytics and Machine Learning Approach for Tsunami Prediction from Satellite and Hydrographic Data
abstract: Tsunamis pose significant threats to coastal regions, necessitating effective disaster preparedness and response efforts. This research project aims to understand and predict tsunami characteristics and arrival time. The first stage involves comprehensive data collection spanning historical earthquake, tsunami, and landslide data from 1800 to 2023. Through reputable databases, scientific publications, historical archives, and government agencies, crucial information on location, magnitude, and timing is gathered. The collected data form the foundation for subsequent analyses and predictions. Leveraging machine learning techniques, including the Random Forest Regressor model and K-means clustering, precise forecasts of tsunami wave speed, travel time, and vulnerability are achieved. Real-time data integration and climate change considerations further enhance prediction capabilities. The research culminates in comprehensive visualizations, including maps highlighting tsunami-prone regions and charts depicting the most affected months. These insights aid disaster management authorities and coastal communities in formulating targeted disaster preparedness and mitigation strategies. The study's global collaboration and advanced predictive models help protect vulnerable areas from tsunamis, offering crucial insights for disaster risk reduction and coastal resilience decision-making.

articleTitle: Modified Feature Selection with BPSO to Apply PSO for Solving Handwritten Digits
abstract: The task of Handwriting Digits Recognition represents a classification challenge involving the interpretation of handwritten digits sourced from diverse mediums such as paper, photos, touch screens, and other devices. This challenge is very intricate due to the distinctiveness of each individual's handwriting, and several essential traits that influence the interpretation process. Numerous researchers have devoted efforts to solve this problem. Recent research has improved preprocessing and feature extraction techniques by using particle swarm optimization to address the handwritten digit recognition problem. The outcomes of these experiments have shown obtain good results. Nevertheless, outcomes from this technique can be further improved. The feature selection technique popularly applies pattern recognition to improve outcomes. Thus, this study proposes a modified feature selection technique that developed from binary particle swarm optimization to optimize particle swarm optimization for handwritten digit recognition. This proposed feature selection technique has demonstrated the potential to yield higher Recognition Rates significantly in both training and testing phases. Comparative analysis against the original technique, devoid of the feature selection technique, reveals that the proposed method exhibits superior Recognition Rates when tested on both the original MNIST datasets and the individual's each person handwritten digit datasets.

articleTitle: Modelling of Power System Restoration of a Synchronous Generator-Driven Network
abstract: A power system blackout is a high-impact but low-probable event. Power system restoration, after a complete blackout, creates substantial challenges for power system operators. To restore the system within a minimum time, the system operators develop and design the system restoration manuals including standards and guidelines. In order to develop these manuals, modelling and simulation tools are required. This paper discusses how to model and simulate a sequential “bottom-up” power system restoration strategy and develop the “power restoration curve”. The restoration curve graphically represents the power exported by the generators over time. It is used to visualize how quickly the black system can be restored. Based on the perspective of the transmission system operator and power plant operator, the modified IEEE 9 bus system was modelled in DIgSILENT Power Factory to model a system restoration. The system focuses on parameters such as black start capability, reactive power capability, frequency, voltage, and load pickup. The power restoration curve has been developed using simulated results. Using these analyses, a sequential strategy is formulated for a safe and efficient power system restoration.

articleTitle: VGGNet Integration for Kidney Tumor Classification
abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs) have recently become more critical diagnostic tools. DCNNs have been shown in previous studies to have performance levels comparable to those of competent medical professionals, mainly when used in the study of kidney cancers. It was especially true when DCNNs were used to investigate kidney tumors. We relied on very complex convolutional networks, also known as very deep convolutional networks (VGGNet), to ensure our study's accuracy and improve the precision of our large-scale image recognition. These networks are also known as very general-purpose gradient-boosting networks. This was done to ensure that the results of our investigation were reliable. After that, these networks were used to examine the Kidney Tumor dataset, which included various symptoms associated with the illness. Our research findings were encouraging because the model demonstrated astonishingly high accuracy rates of one hundred percent for categorizing normal, cyst, stone, and tumor, respectively. It offered a great deal of solace at difficult times. In the realm of medical diagnostics, a significant new development has just recently been finished being implemented.

articleTitle: Hybridization Harris Hawk Optimization and β-Hill Climbing for Voxel Selection in Brain Decoding
abstract: Decoding visual stimuli is a growingly significant neuroscience task. The objective is to categorize the brain's activity during the perceptron of visual items. The outputs are the names of the stimuli, while the inputs are functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data. Selecting informative features (voxels) is one of the key challenges facing in the brain decoder. We propose the hybrid Harris hawk voxel selection (HHHVS) algorithm to precisely decode the brain activity induced by visual stimuli. This inspired us to develop a better version of Harris hawk optimization algorithm that includes (β-hill climbing to maximize the exploration procedure. An effective final voxel is evaluated using support vector machine classifier and six (6) well-known metaheuristic algorithms. The obtained outcomes are beyond the other metaheuristic algorithms in terms of number of selected voxels, classification accuracy, standard deviation, and convergence speed. The experimental findings of the proposed technique are highly encouraging and can be employed successfully in the brain computer interface system.
